bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: =漢紀五十三=起瘀逢閹茂，盡旃蒙大淵獻，凡二年。

translations.literal: 【Han Records 53】 Beginning from Yufeng Yanmao through Zhanmeng Dayuanxian—in all, two years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Han Records 53】 From the year Yufeng Yanmao through Zhanmeng Dayuanxian—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，辛酉，赦天下。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on the day xinyou, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on xinyou day, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 2甲子，帝加元服。

translations.literal: 2 On jiazi day, the Emperor performed the capping ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day, the emperor came of age and assumed full adult status.

sentences.zh: 3二月，戊寅，有司奏立長秋宮。

translations.literal: 3 In the second month, on the day wuyin, the relevant officials memorialized to establish the empress in the Changqiu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuyin day, the responsible offices submitted a memorial proposing the selection of an empress for the Changqiu Palace.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「皇妣宅兆未卜，何忍言後宮之選乎！

translations.literal: An edict said: "The burial site of the late Empress Dowager has not yet been chosen; how can we bear to speak of selecting for the rear palace!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed: "My late mother's burial site has not yet been chosen—how can I bear to discuss selecting someone for the inner palace!

sentences.zh: 」壬午，三公奏改葬皇妣王夫人，追上尊號曰靈懷皇后。

translations.literal: " On renwu day, the Three Ducal Ministers memorialized to reinter the late Empress Dowager Lady Wang and bestow the posthumous honorific title Spirit-Commiserating Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day, the Three Ducal Ministers petitioned to rebury the late Lady Wang with full honors and confer upon her the posthumous title Empress Linghuai.

sentences.zh: 4陶謙告急於田楷，楷與平原相劉備救之。

translations.literal: 4 Tao Qian sent an urgent appeal to Tian Kai; Kai, together with Liu Bei, prefect of Pingyuan, went to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian sent an urgent appeal for help to Tian Kai, who marched to his aid together with Liu Bei, the prefect of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 備自有兵數千人，謙益以丹陽兵四千，備遂去楷歸謙，謙表為豫州刺史，屯小沛。

translations.literal: Bei already had several thousand troops of his own; Qian augmented these with four thousand Danyang soldiers. Bei thereupon left Kai and returned to Qian's service. Qian recommended him as Inspector of Yuzhou and quartered him at Xiaopei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei already commanded several thousand men of his own; Tao Qian added four thousand Danyang troops to his force. Bei then left Tian Kai and entered Qian's service. Qian recommended him as Inspector of Yuzhou and stationed him at Xiaopei.

sentences.zh: 曹操軍食亦盡，引兵還。

translations.literal: Cao Cao's army provisions were also exhausted, and he led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's army had also run out of provisions, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 5馬騰私有求於李傕，不獲而怒，欲舉兵相攻；

translations.literal: 5 Ma Teng had made a private request of Li Jue; when it was not granted he grew angry and wished to raise troops to attack him;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng had made a private request of Li Jue; when it was refused he flew into a rage and prepared to raise troops against him;

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者和解之，不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to mediate, but they were not obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to broker peace, but neither side would listen.

sentences.zh: 韓遂率眾來和騰、傕，即而復與騰合。

translations.literal: Han Sui led his followers to reconcile Teng and Jue, but then joined with Teng again.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui brought his followers to mediate between Teng and Jue, but soon allied himself with Teng once more.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫种邵、侍中馬宇、左中郎將劉範謀使騰襲長安，己為內應，以誅傕等。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Discourse Grandee Zhong Shao, Palace Attendant Ma Yu, and Left Commandant of the Guards Liu Fan plotted to have Teng raid Chang'an, with themselves as inside collaborators, in order to execute Jue and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Discourse Grandee Zhong Shao, Palace Attendant Ma Yu, and Left Commandant of the Guards Liu Fan plotted to have Ma Teng strike at Chang'an while they served as inside collaborators, intending to kill Li Jue and his faction.

sentences.zh: 壬申<ref>壬申是年二月戊寅朔，無壬申。

translations.literal: On renshen day [ref]: In this year the second month begins on wuyin; there is no renshen day.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day [editorial note]: That year the second month opened on wuyin, so there was no renshen day.

sentences.zh: 據《後漢書．獻帝紀》，此事擊於三月，惟三月戊申朔，無壬申。

translations.literal: According to the Annals of Emperor Xian in the Book of Later Han, this event is recorded in the third month; but the third month begins on wushen, and there is no renshen day.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Annals of Emperor Xian in the Book of Later Han, the event belongs in the third month; yet the third month opened on wushen, and again there was no renshen day.

sentences.zh: </ref>，騰、遂勒兵屯長平觀。

translations.literal: </ref> Teng and Sui mustered troops and encamped at Changping Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Teng and Sui assembled their forces and encamped at Changping Guan.

sentences.zh: 邵等謀泄，出奔槐里。

translations.literal: Shao and the others' plot leaked out; they fled to Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao and his co-conspirators' plot was exposed, they fled to Huaili.

sentences.zh: 傕使樊稠、郭汜及兄子利擊之，騰、遂敗走，還涼州。

translations.literal: Jue sent Fan Chou, Guo Si, and his nephew Li to attack them. Teng and Sui were defeated and fled back to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue dispatched Fan Chou, Guo Si, and his nephew Li against them. Teng and Sui were routed and fled back to Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 又攻槐里，邵等皆死。

translations.literal: They also attacked Huaili, and Shao and the others were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: They then attacked Huaili as well, and Shao and his fellows were all killed.

sentences.zh: 庚申<ref>庚申是年二月戊寅朔，無庚申。

translations.literal: On gengshen day [ref]: In this year the second month begins on wuyin; there is no gengshen day.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day [editorial note]: That year the second month opened on wuyin, so there was no gengshen day.

sentences.zh: 據《後漢書．獻帝紀》，此事擊於三月，為農曆十三日。

translations.literal: According to the Annals of Emperor Xian in the Book of Later Han, this event is recorded in the third month, on the thirteenth day of the agricultural calendar.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Annals of Emperor Xian in the Book of Later Han, the event took place in the third month, on the thirteenth day.

sentences.zh: </ref>，詔赦騰等。

translations.literal: </ref> An edict granted amnesty to Teng and the others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued granting amnesty to Teng and his followers.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以騰為安狄將軍，遂為安降將軍。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Teng was appointed General Who Pacifies the Di, and Sui was appointed General Who Pacifies Surrenders.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Ma Teng was made General Who Pacifies the Di, and Han Sui was made General Who Pacifies Surrenders.

sentences.zh: 6曹操使司馬荀彧、壽張令程昱守鄄城，復往攻陶謙，遂略地至琅邪、東海，所過殘滅。

translations.literal: 6 Cao Cao left Major Xun Yu and Shouzhang magistrate Cheng Yu to defend Juancheng, then again marched to attack Tao Qian. He overran territory as far as Langye and Donghai, laying waste everywhere he passed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao left Major Xun Yu and Shouzhang magistrate Cheng Yu to hold Juancheng, then marched again against Tao Qian. He swept through the countryside as far as Langye and Donghai, leaving devastation in his wake.

sentences.zh: 還，擊破劉備於郯東。

translations.literal: On the return march he defeated Liu Bei east of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he routed Liu Bei east of Tan.

sentences.zh: 謙恐，欲走歸丹陽。

translations.literal: Qian was afraid and wished to flee back to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian was terrified and prepared to flee back to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 會陳留太守張邈叛操迎呂布，操乃引軍還。

translations.literal: Just then Chenliu Administrator Zhang Miao rebelled against Cao and welcomed Lü Bu, so Cao led his army back.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Chenliu Administrator Zhang Miao turned against Cao Cao and welcomed Lü Bu, and Cao was forced to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 初，張邈少時，好遊俠，袁紹、曹操皆與之善。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Miao was young, he loved wandering knight-errantry; both Yuan Shao and Cao Cao were on good terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Zhang Miao had been a wandering knight-errant, and both Yuan Shao and Cao Cao counted him as a friend.

sentences.zh: 及紹為盟主，有驕色，邈正議責紹；

translations.literal: When Shao became alliance leader he showed arrogance, and Miao openly criticized and rebuked him in debate;
translations.idiomatic: Once Shao became head of the coalition he grew arrogant, and Miao openly rebuked him in council;

sentences.zh: 紹怒，使操殺之。

translations.literal: Shao was angered and had Cao kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was furious and ordered Cao Cao to kill him.

sentences.zh: 操不聽，曰：「孟卓，親友也，是非當容之。

translations.literal: Cao would not listen, saying: "Mengzhuo is kin and friend; right and wrong should be tolerated in his case.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao refused, saying, "Mengzhuo is a close friend—one must make allowances for a man's faults.

sentences.zh: 今天下未定，奈何自相危也！

translations.literal: The realm is not yet settled—how can we turn on each other!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is not yet settled—why turn on one another now!

sentences.zh: 」操之前攻陶謙，志在必死，敕家曰：「我若不還，往依孟卓。

translations.literal: " When Cao had previously attacked Tao Qian, determined to fight to the death, he instructed his household: "If I do not return, go and rely on Mengzhuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao had earlier marched against Tao Qian, prepared to fight to the death, he told his household, "If I do not return, go to Mengzhuo for refuge.

sentences.zh: 」後還見邈，垂泣相對。

translations.literal: " Later, when he returned and saw Miao, they faced each other in tears.
translations.idiomatic: When he later returned and saw Miao again, the two men wept face to face.

sentences.zh: 陳留高柔謂鄉人曰：「曹操軍雖據兗州，本有四方之圖，未得安坐守也。

translations.literal: Gao Rou of Chenliu said to his fellow townsmen: "Although Cao Cao's army holds Yan Province, he originally had designs on all four directions and cannot sit quietly and merely defend.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou of Chenliu told his neighbors, "Cao Cao may hold Yan Province, but his ambitions extend in every direction—he cannot simply sit back and defend what he has.

sentences.zh: 而張府君恃陳留之資，將乘間為變，欲與諸君避之，何如？

translations.literal: Yet Administrator Zhang relies on Chenliu's resources and will seize an opportunity to rebel. I wish to leave with all of you and avoid the coming trouble—what do you say?
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Zhang has Chenliu's wealth behind him and will seize the first chance to turn against Cao. I mean to leave with my kin and avoid what is coming—will you join me?

sentences.zh: 」眾人皆以曹、張相親，柔又年少，不然其言。

translations.literal: " Everyone thought Cao and Zhang were close, and since Rou was still young, they did not believe his words.
translations.idiomatic: The others dismissed the warning: Cao and Zhang were close friends, and besides, Rou was still young.

sentences.zh: 柔從兄幹自河北呼柔，柔舉宗從之。

translations.literal: Rou's older clansman cousin Gan summoned him from Hebei, and Rou moved his entire clan to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Rou's elder cousin Gan summoned him from Hebei, and Rou took his whole clan and went.

sentences.zh: 呂布之捨袁紹從張楊也，過邈，臨別，把手共誓。

translations.literal: When Lü Bu left Yuan Shao to join Zhang Yang, he passed through Miao's territory; on parting they clasped hands and swore an oath together.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Bu abandoned Yuan Shao to follow Zhang Yang, he passed through Miao's domain; on parting the two clasped hands and swore a bond together.

sentences.zh: 紹聞之，大恨。

translations.literal: When Shao heard of this, he was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao heard of this, he was furious.

sentences.zh: 邈畏操終為紹殺己也，心不自安。

translations.literal: Miao feared that Cao would eventually kill him at Shao's behest, and his heart was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Miao feared that Cao Cao would eventually kill him at Shao's urging, and he grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 前九江太守陳留邊讓嘗譏議操，操聞而殺之，並其妻子。

translations.literal: Former Jiujiang Administrator Bian Rang of Chenliu had once mocked and criticized Cao; when Cao heard of it he killed him, together with his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Former Jiujiang Administrator Bian Rang of Chenliu had once ridiculed Cao Cao in public; when Cao learned of it he had him killed, along with his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 讓素有才名，由是兗州士大夫皆恐懼。

translations.literal: Rang had long enjoyed a reputation for talent, and from this the gentry and officials of Yan Province were all filled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Rang had been a man of celebrated talent, and the affair left the scholars and officials of Yan Province terrified.

sentences.zh: 陳宮性剛直壯烈，內亦自疑，乃與從事中郎許汜、王楷及邈弟超共謀叛操。

translations.literal: Chen Gong was by nature stern, upright, and fierce; inwardly he too was suspicious, and so together with Attendant of Affairs Xu Si, Wang Kai, and Miao's younger brother Chao he plotted to rebel against Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong was a man of fierce, uncompromising integrity, and he too began to doubt Cao Cao. Together with Attendant of Affairs Xu Si and Wang Kai, and with Miao's younger brother Chao, he plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 宮說邈曰：「今天下分崩，雄傑並起，君以千里之眾，當四戰之地，撫劍顧眄，亦足以為人豪，而反受制於人，不亦鄙乎！

translations.literal: Gong said to Miao: "Today the realm is splitting apart and heroes are rising together. You command followers across a thousand li and hold a land contested on four sides; with a hand on your sword and a glance about you, you are enough to be a lord among men—yet you submit to another's control. Is that not contemptible!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong urged Miao: "The realm is breaking apart and heroes are rising on every side. You command thousands across a thousand li in a land fought over from every direction—hand on your sword, you could be a lord among men. Yet you let yourself be ruled by another. Is that not shameful!

sentences.zh: 今州軍東征，其處空虛，呂布壯士，善戰無前，若權迎之，共牧兗州，觀天下形勢，俟時事之變，此亦縱橫之一時也。

translations.literal: Now the provincial army is campaigning eastward and this place is empty. Lü Bu is a fierce warrior, unmatched in battle; if for the moment you welcome him and together govern Yan Province, watch the shape of affairs under Heaven, and await the turn of events—this too would be a moment for alliance politics.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial army is away campaigning east, and the heartland is undefended. Lü Bu is a fierce fighter without equal—welcome him for now, rule Yan Province together, watch how the realm unfolds, and wait for the moment to act. That would be your chance to play the great game.

sentences.zh: 」邈從之。

translations.literal: " Miao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Miao agreed.

sentences.zh: 時操使宮將兵留屯東郡，遂以其眾潛迎布為兗州牧。

translations.literal: At the time Cao had assigned Gong to command troops garrisoned in Dongjun, and so with those forces he secretly welcomed Bu as Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had left Chen Gong in command of a garrison at Dongjun, and Gong used those troops to secretly install Lü Bu as Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 布至，邈乃使其黨劉翊告荀彧曰：「呂將軍業助曹使君擊陶謙，宜亟供其軍食。

translations.literal: When Bu arrived, Miao sent his partisan Liu Yi to tell Xun Yu: "General Lü has already come to assist Lord Cao in attacking Tao Qian; you should promptly supply his army with provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Bu arrived, Miao sent his ally Liu Yi to tell Xun Yu, "General Lü has come to help Lord Cao against Tao Qian—you should send provisions at once.

sentences.zh: 」眾疑惑，彧知邈為亂，即勒兵設備，急召東郡太守夏侯惇於濮陽；

translations.literal: " The crowd was puzzled. Yu knew Miao was rebelling, and at once mustered troops and made preparations, urgently summoning Dongjun Administrator Xiahou Dun from Puyang;
translations.idiomatic: The men were bewildered. Xun Yu saw that Miao had rebelled, immediately mustered the garrison, and urgently summoned Dongjun Administrator Xiahou Dun from Puyang.

sentences.zh: 惇來，布遂據濮陽。

translations.literal: Before Dun arrived, Bu seized Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xiahou Dun could arrive, Lü Bu took Puyang.

sentences.zh: 時操悉軍攻陶謙，留守兵少，而督將、大吏多與邈、宮通謀。

translations.literal: At the time Cao had committed his entire army to attacking Tao Qian, leaving few troops behind, and many supervising generals and senior officials were in secret communication with Miao and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had taken nearly his entire army against Tao Qian, leaving only a skeleton force behind, and many of the senior officers and officials were already in contact with Miao and Chen Gong.

sentences.zh: 惇至，其夜，誅謀叛者數十人，眾乃定。

translations.literal: When Dun arrived, that night he executed several dozen plotters, and the troops were finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiahou Dun arrived, he executed several dozen conspirators that same night, and order was at last restored.

sentences.zh: 豫州剌史郭貢率眾數萬來至城下，或言與呂布同謀，眾甚懼。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yuzhou Guo Gong led several tens of thousands of followers to the foot of the city walls. Some said he was in league with Lü Bu, and the troops were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yuzhou Guo Gong marched tens of thousands of men to the city walls. Rumors spread that he was in league with Lü Bu, and fear swept through the garrison.

sentences.zh: 貢求見荀彧，彧將往，惇等曰：「君一州鎮也，往必危，不可。

translations.literal: Gong requested an audience with Xun Yu. Yu was about to go when Dun and the others said: "You are the pillar of the province; if you go you will surely be in danger—it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Gong asked to meet Xun Yu. Yu was about to go when Xiahou Dun and the others protested: "You are the linchpin of the province—if you go, you will be in mortal danger.

sentences.zh: 」彧曰：「貢與邈等，分非素結也，今來速，計必未定，及其未定說之，縱不為用，可使中立。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Gong and Miao and the others are not old allies by nature. He has come quickly, so his plans cannot yet be settled. While they are still unsettled I shall persuade him; even if he will not be used by us, we can make him remain neutral.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu replied, "Guo Gong is no longtime ally of Miao and the rest. He arrived in haste, so his plans cannot be firm yet. If I speak to him before he decides, I may not win him over—but I can at least keep him neutral.

sentences.zh: 若先疑之，彼將怒而成計。

translations.literal: If we suspect him first, he will grow angry and settle on a plan.
translations.idiomatic: If we show suspicion first, he will take offense and commit to their side.

sentences.zh: 」貢見彧無懼意，謂鄄城未易攻，遂引兵去。

translations.literal: " When Gong saw that Yu showed no fear, he judged Juancheng would not be easy to take, and led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Gong saw that Xun Yu showed no fear, he decided Juancheng would not fall easily and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是時，兗州郡縣皆應布，唯鄄城、范、東阿不動。

translations.literal: At this time the commanderies and counties of Yan Province all responded to Bu; only Juancheng, Fan, and Dong'e held firm.
translations.idiomatic: By then every county in Yan Province had declared for Lü Bu—only Juancheng, Fan, and Dong'e held out.

sentences.zh: 布軍降者言：「陳宮欲自將兵取東阿，又使氾嶷取范。

translations.literal: Defectors from Bu's army said: "Chen Gong intends to lead troops himself to take Dong'e, and has also sent Fan Yi to take Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Deserters from Lü Bu's camp reported that Chen Gong meant to lead troops personally against Dong'e and had sent Fan Yi to seize Fan.

sentences.zh: 」吏民皆恐。

translations.literal: " Officials and commoners alike were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike were terrified.

sentences.zh: 程昱本東阿人，彧謂昱曰：「今舉州皆叛，唯有此三城，宮等以重兵臨之，非有以深結其心，三城必動。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu was originally a man of Dong'e. Xun Yu said to Cheng Yu: "Now the whole province has rebelled; only these three cities remain. Gong and the others are pressing them with heavy forces—unless we can deeply bind their hearts, the three cities will surely waver.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu was a native of Dong'e. Xun Yu told him, "The whole province has turned against us except these three cities. Chen Gong is bearing down on them with a large army—unless we win their loyalty completely, all three will fall.

sentences.zh: 君，民之望也，宜往撫之。

translations.literal: You are the people's hope; you should go and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: You are the man the people look to—you should go and rally them.

sentences.zh: 」昱乃歸過范，說其令靳允曰：「聞呂布執君母、弟、妻子，孝子誠不可為心。

translations.literal: " Yu then returned by way of Fan and persuaded its magistrate Jin Yun, saying: "I hear that Lü Bu holds your mother, younger brother, wife, and children. A filial son truly cannot bear this in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu set out for home by way of Fan and spoke to its magistrate, Jin Yun: "I hear Lü Bu holds your mother, brother, wife, and children. No filial son could bear that.

sentences.zh: 今天下大亂，英雄並起，必有命世能息天下之亂者，此智者所宜詳擇也。

translations.literal: Today the realm is in great disorder and heroes are rising together; there must be one destined to still the chaos of the realm—this is what the wise should carefully choose.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in chaos and heroes are rising on every side. One man is destined to end the turmoil—that is whom the wise must choose with care.

sentences.zh: 得主者昌，失主者亡。

translations.literal: Those who gain the right lord flourish; those who lose him perish.
translations.idiomatic: Those who back the right leader prosper; those who choose wrong are destroyed.

sentences.zh: 陳宮叛迎呂布而百城皆應，似能有為；

translations.literal: Chen Gong rebelled and welcomed Lü Bu, and a hundred cities responded—it seems he could accomplish something;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong rebelled and welcomed Lü Bu, and a hundred cities rallied to them—it looks as though they might succeed;

sentences.zh: 然以君觀之，布何如人哉？

translations.literal: yet in your judgment, what sort of man is Bu?
translations.idiomatic: but in your judgment, what sort of man is Lü Bu?

sentences.zh: 夫布粗中少親，剛而無禮，匹夫之雄耳。

translations.literal: Bu is coarse within and lacking in affection, fierce yet without propriety—merely a hero of the common man.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu is brutish and faithless, fierce but without restraint—the hero of a common brawler, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 宮等以勢假合，不能相君也；

translations.literal: Gong and the others have joined him only by borrowed force and cannot truly serve as your lord;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong and the rest have rallied to him only for the moment—they cannot truly make him your master;

sentences.zh: 兵雖眾，終必無成。

translations.literal: though their troops are many, in the end they will surely accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: however many troops they field, they will come to nothing in the end.

sentences.zh: 曹使君智略不世出，殆天所授。

translations.literal: Lord Cao's stratagems are unmatched in the age—he is perhaps Heaven's chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao's genius is unmatched in our age—he may well be Heaven's chosen man.

sentences.zh: 君必固范，我守東阿，則田單之功可立也。

translations.literal: If you hold Fan firm and I defend Dong'e, then the achievement of Tian Dan can be established.
translations.idiomatic: Hold Fan firm while I defend Dong'e, and we can repeat Tian Dan's feat at Jimo.

sentences.zh: 孰與違忠從惡而母子俱亡乎？

translations.literal: How does that compare with turning from loyalty to follow evil, so that mother and son perish together?
translations.idiomatic: Surely that is better than abandoning loyalty for treason and losing your whole family?

sentences.zh: 唯君詳慮之！

translations.literal: I ask only that you consider this carefully!
translations.idiomatic: Think it through carefully!

sentences.zh: 」允流涕曰：「不敢有貳心。

translations.literal: " Yun wept and said: "I dare not harbor a second heart.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yun wept and said, "I will not waver in my loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」時泛嶷已在縣，允乃見嶷，伏兵刺殺之，歸，勒兵自守。

translations.literal: " At the time Fan Yi was already in the county. Yun then went to see Yi, had hidden troops stab and kill him, returned, and mustered the troops to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yi was already in the county. Yun went out to meet him, had concealed soldiers cut him down, then returned and rallied the garrison to hold the city.

sentences.zh: ::徐眾評曰：允於曹公未成君臣；

translations.literal: :: Xu Zhong's commentary says: Yun had not yet become lord and minister with Lord Cao;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhong comments: Jin Yun was not yet bound to Lord Cao as lord and minister;

sentences.zh: 母至親也，於義應去。

translations.literal: a mother is one's closest kin, and by right he should have gone to her.
translations.idiomatic: a mother is one's closest kin, and by every moral rule he should have gone to save her.

sentences.zh: 衛公子開方仕齊，積年不返，管仲以為不懷其親，安能愛君！

translations.literal: The Wei prince's son Kaifang served in Qi and for years did not return; Guan Zhong held that one who does not cherish his kin—how could he love his lord!
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei prince's son Kaifang entered Qi's service and stayed away for years, Guan Zhong said that a man who does not cherish his own kin cannot truly love his lord.

sentences.zh: 是以求忠臣必於孝子之門；

translations.literal: Therefore in seeking loyal ministers one must look among filial sons;
translations.idiomatic: That is why loyal ministers are sought among filial sons;

sentences.zh: 允宜先救至親。

translations.literal: Yun ought first to have rescued his closest kin.
translations.idiomatic: Yun should first have rescued his family.

sentences.zh: 徐庶母為曹公所得，劉備遣庶歸北，欲為天下者恕人子之情也；

translations.literal: When Xu Shu's mother was taken by Lord Cao, Liu Bei sent Shu back north—one who would win the realm must forgive a son's feelings;
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shu's mother fell into Lord Cao's hands, Liu Bei sent Xu Shu home—a man who would rule the realm must respect a son's duty to his mother;

sentences.zh: 曹公亦宜遣允。

translations.literal: Lord Cao too ought to have sent Yun away.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao should likewise have released Yun to his family.

sentences.zh: 7昱又遣別騎絕倉亭津，陳宮至，不得渡。

translations.literal: 7 Yu also sent separate cavalry to block Cangting Ford; when Chen Gong arrived, he could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu also sent a detachment of cavalry to hold Cangting Ford, blocking Chen Gong when he arrived.

sentences.zh: 昱至東阿，東阿令潁川棗祗已率厲吏民拒城堅守，卒完三城以待操。

translations.literal: When Yu reached Dong'e, Dong'e magistrate Zao Zhi of Yingchuan had already rallied officials and commoners to defend the city resolutely, and in the end the three cities were preserved intact to await Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Yu reached Dong'e, its magistrate Zao Zhi of Yingchuan had already rallied officials and townspeople to hold the walls. In the end all three cities stood firm until Cao Cao returned.

sentences.zh: 操還，執昱手曰：「微子之力，吾無所歸矣。

translations.literal: When Cao returned, he took Yu's hand and said: "But for your strength, I would have had nowhere to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao returned, he took Cheng Yu's hand and said, "Without you, I would have had nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 」表昱為東平相，屯范。

translations.literal: " He recommended Yu as Administrator of Dongping and quartered him at Fan.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Cheng Yu as Administrator of Dongping and stationed him at Fan.

sentences.zh: 呂布攻鄄城不能下，西屯濮陽。

translations.literal: Lü Bu attacked Juancheng but could not take it, and encamped west at Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu failed to take Juancheng and withdrew west to encamp at Puyang.

sentences.zh: 曹操曰：「布一旦得一州，不能據東平，斷亢父、泰山之道，乘險要我，而乃屯濮陽，吾知其無能為也。

translations.literal: Cao Cao said: "Bu suddenly gained a whole province, yet could not hold Dongping, cut the road through Kangfu and Mount Tai, and use the terrain to threaten me—instead he encamps at Puyang. I know he can accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Lü Bu suddenly seized a whole province, yet instead of holding Dongping, cutting the Kangfu–Mount Tai road, and using the terrain to block me, he camps at Puyang. I know he will come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 」乃進攻之。

translations.literal: " He then advanced to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched to attack him.

sentences.zh: 8五月，以揚武將軍郭汜為後將軍，安集將軍樊稠為右將軍，並開府如三公，合為六府，皆參選舉。

translations.literal: 8 In the fifth month, General Who Displays Martiality Guo Si was made General of the Rear, and General Who Pacifies and Gathers Fan Chou was made General of the Right; each opened an office like the Three Ducal Ministers, making six offices in all, all participating in selections and recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Guo Si was promoted from General Who Displays Martiality to General of the Rear, and Fan Chou from General Who Pacifies and Gathers to General of the Right. Each was granted an office equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, bringing the total to six such offices, all with a hand in appointments.

sentences.zh: 李傕等各欲用其所舉，若一違之，便忿憤喜怒。

translations.literal: Li Jue and the others each wished to employ those they had recommended; if anyone went against them even once, they would flare up in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his faction each insisted on appointing their own nominees; the slightest refusal sent them into a rage.

sentences.zh: 主者患之，乃以次第用其所舉。

translations.literal: Those in charge were troubled by this and therefore employed their recommendations in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The officials in charge, at a loss, began appointing their nominees in rotation.

sentences.zh: 先從傕起，汜次之，稠次之，三公所舉，終不見用。

translations.literal: They began with Jue's recommendations, then Si's, then Chou's; those recommended by the Three Ducal Ministers were never employed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue's nominees came first, then Guo Si's, then Fan Chou's; candidates put forward by the Three Ducal Ministers were never appointed.

sentences.zh: 9河西四郡以去涼州治遠，隔以河寇，上書求別置州。

translations.literal: 9 The four commanderies west of the Yellow River, because they were far from the seat of Liang Province and cut off by river bandits, submitted a memorial requesting that a separate province be established.
translations.idiomatic: The four commanderies west of the Yellow River petitioned to be made a separate province, citing their distance from the Liang Province capital and the river bandits that cut them off.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙子，詔以陳留邯鄲商為雍州剌史，典治之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day bingzi, an edict appointed Handan Shang of Chenliu as Inspector of Yong Province to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingzi day, an edict appointed Handan Shang of Chenliu Inspector of Yong Province to govern the new province.

sentences.zh: 10丁丑，京師地震；

translations.literal: 10 On the day dingchou, the capital region was shaken by an earthquake;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day, the capital was shaken by an earthquake;

sentences.zh: 戊寅，又震。

translations.literal: on wuyin day it shook again.
translations.idiomatic: on wuyin day it shook again.

translations.idiomatic: 11 On yi [si] day (

translations.idiomatic: yiyou)

translations.literal: [The last day of the] month: in this year the sixth month begins on bingzi; the last day of the month is yisi. The Annals of Emperor Xian in the Book of Later Han has yisi correctly; amended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note: In this year the sixth month begins on bingzi, making the last day yisi. The Annals of Emperor Xian in the Book of Later Han reads yisi; the text is amended accordingly.

translations.literal: </ref>; there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: —there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 12秋，七月，壬子，太尉朱儁免。

translations.literal: 12 In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renzi, Grand Commandant Zhu Jun was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on renzi day, Zhu Jun was removed from office as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 13戊午，以太常楊彪為太尉，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: 13 On wuwu day, the Grand Minister of Ceremonies Yang Biao was made Grand Commandant and put in charge of affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day, Yang Biao, Grand Minister of Ceremonies, was appointed Grand Commandant and entrusted with oversight of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 14甲子，以鎮南將軍楊定為安西將軍，開府如三公。

translations.literal: 14 On jiazi day, General Who Subdues the South Yang Ding was made General Who Pacifies the West, with an office opened like the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day, Yang Ding, General Who Subdues the South, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West and granted an office equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 15自四月不雨至於是月，穀一斛值錢五十萬，長安中人相食。

translations.literal: 15 From the fourth month there had been no rain until this month; a hu of grain was worth five hundred thousand cash, and people in Chang'an ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: No rain had fallen since the fourth month. By now a bushel of grain cost five hundred thousand coins, and in Chang'an people were eating one another.

sentences.zh: 帝令侍御史侯汶出太倉米豆為貧人作糜，餓死者如故。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Palace Attendant Hou Wen to issue grain and beans from the great granary to cook porridge for the poor, but people still died of starvation as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Palace Attendant Hou Wen to distribute grain and beans from the imperial granary and cook porridge for the destitute—but the starving died just the same.

sentences.zh: 帝疑稟賦不實，取米豆各五升於御前作糜，得二盆。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected the rations were not honestly measured; he took five sheng of grain and five sheng of beans each before him and cooked porridge, obtaining only two bowls.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting fraud, the emperor had five liters of grain and five liters of beans brought before him and cooked into porridge himself—it yielded only two bowls.

sentences.zh: 乃杖汶五十，於是悉得全濟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had Wen beaten fifty strokes, and then all were fully saved and relieved.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wen flogged fifty strokes; from then on every ration was delivered in full and the people were saved.

sentences.zh: 16八月，馮翊羌寇屬縣，郭汜、樊稠等率眾破之。

translations.literal: 16 In the eighth month, Qiang of Fengyi raided dependent counties; Guo Si, Fan Chou, and others led forces and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Qiang raiders from Fengyi attacked outlying counties. Guo Si, Fan Chou, and others took the field and routed them.

sentences.zh: 17呂布有別屯在濮陽西，曹操夜襲破之，未及還。

translations.literal: 17 Lü Bu had a separate encampment west of Puyang; Cao Cao raided it by night and broke it, but had not yet returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu maintained a separate camp west of Puyang. Cao Cao made a night attack and smashed it but had not yet withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 會布至，身自搏戰，自旦至日，數十合，相持甚急。

translations.literal: Just then Bu arrived; he personally joined the fighting himself. From dawn until sundown they exchanged blows dozens of times; the stalemate was extremely tense.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu arrived in person and took the field himself. From dawn until dusk they clashed dozens of times, locked in a desperate standoff.

sentences.zh: 操募人陷陣，司馬陳留典韋將應募者進當之，布弓弩亂髮，矢至如雨。

translations.literal: Cao Cao recruited men to break the enemy line; Major Dian Wei of Chenliu led the volunteers forward to meet them. Bu's bowmen and crossbowmen loosed arrows until their hair was tangled; the arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao called for volunteers to punch through the enemy line. Major Dian Wei of Chenliu led the recruits forward. Lü Bu's archers poured arrows down until their hair was tangled with bowstrings; shafts fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 韋不視，謂等人曰：「虜來十步，乃白之。

translations.literal: Wei did not look; he said to the others: "When the enemy comes within ten paces, then report it to me.
translations.idiomatic: Wei never glanced up. He told his men, "Wait until the enemy is ten paces away—then tell me.

sentences.zh: 」等人曰：「十步矣。

translations.literal: " The others said: "Ten paces already.
translations.idiomatic: "They said, "Ten paces!

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「五步乃白。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Five paces—then report.
translations.idiomatic: "He said, "Not until five paces.

sentences.zh: 」等人懼，疾言「虜至矣！

translations.literal: " The others were afraid and cried in haste, "The enemy is here!
translations.idiomatic: "Terrified, they shouted, "They're on us!

sentences.zh: 」韋持戟大呼而起，所抵無不應手倒者，布眾退。

translations.literal: " Wei took up his halberd, leaped up with a great shout; every foe he struck fell at the blow, and Bu's troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: "Wei seized his halberd, roared, and sprang forward. Every man he struck went down at once, and Lü Bu's forces fell back.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，操乃得引去。

translations.literal: At sundown Cao Cao was finally able to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Cao Cao was finally able to pull his forces out.

sentences.zh: 拜韋都尉，令常將親兵數百人，繞大帳左右。

translations.literal: Wei was appointed Commandant and ordered always to lead several hundred personal troops circling the main tent.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao appointed Dian Wei Commandant and posted several hundred elite guards under his command around the headquarters tent.

sentences.zh: 濮陽大姓田氏為反間，操得入城，燒其東門，示無反意。

translations.literal: The great clan Tian of Puyang acted as a double agent for Cao Cao; Cao was able to enter the city, burn its east gate, and show that he had no intention of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful Tian clan of Puyang worked as a double agent for Cao Cao, letting him into the city. He burned the east gate to signal that he had no intent to rebel.

sentences.zh: 及戰，軍敗，布騎得操而不識，問曰：「曹操何在？

translations.literal: When battle was joined the army was defeated; Bu's cavalry captured Cao Cao but did not recognize him and asked: "Where is Cao Cao?
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting Cao Cao's army was beaten. Lü Bu's horsemen seized a man they did not recognize and demanded, "Where is Cao Cao?

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「乘黃馬走者是也。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao said: "The one riding away on the yellow horse is he.
translations.idiomatic: "Cao Cao pointed and said, "The man fleeing on the yellow horse—that's Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 」布騎乃釋操而追黃馬者。

translations.literal: " Bu's cavalry thereupon released Cao Cao and pursued the man on the yellow horse.
translations.idiomatic: "They released him and galloped after the rider on the yellow horse.

sentences.zh: 操突火而出，至營，自力勞軍，令軍中促為攻具，進，復攻之，與布相守百餘日。

translations.literal: Cao Cao broke through the fire and came out, reached his camp, personally exhorted the army, ordered the troops to speed the making of siege equipment, advanced, and attacked again; he and Bu held each other off for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao burst through the flames, reached camp, and rallied the troops himself. He ordered siege equipment built at once and pressed the attack again. He and Lü Bu remained deadlocked for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 蝗蟲起，百姓大餓，布糧食亦盡，各引去。

translations.literal: Locusts appeared; the common people were greatly famine-stricken; Bu's grain was also exhausted; each side withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts swarmed; famine gripped the countryside; Lü Bu's supplies ran out. Both armies broke off.

sentences.zh: 九月，操還鄄城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Cao Cao returned to Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Cao Cao withdrew to Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 布到乘氏，為其縣人李進所破，東屯山陽。

translations.literal: Bu went to Chengshi and was defeated by the county man Li Jin; he encamped east at Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu withdrew to Chengshi, where he was beaten by Li Jin of that county, then moved east to encamp at Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，操至東阿。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Cao Cao went to Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Cao Cao marched to Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 袁紹使人說操，欲使操遣家居鄴。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao sent someone to persuade Cao Cao, wishing to have Cao send his family to reside at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent envoys urging Cao Cao to send his household to live at Ye.

sentences.zh: 操新失兗州，軍食盡，將許之，程昱曰：「意者將軍殆臨事而懼，不然，何慮之不深也！

translations.literal: Cao Cao had newly lost Yan Province and his army provisions were exhausted; he was about to agree when Cheng Yu said: "It seems, General, you are perhaps afraid in facing events—or else why do you not think more deeply!
translations.idiomatic: Freshly stripped of Yan Province and out of provisions, Cao Cao was ready to agree when Cheng Yu protested, "General, you seem frightened by the crisis at hand—otherwise why would you think so shallowly?

sentences.zh: 夫袁紹有併天下之心，而智不能濟也；

translations.literal: Yuan Shao has the mind to swallow all under Heaven, yet his wisdom cannot carry it through;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao means to swallow the empire whole, but his talents cannot finish the job;

sentences.zh: 將軍自度能為之下乎？

translations.literal: can you, General, measure yourself and serve under him?
translations.idiomatic: do you really think you can bow to him?

sentences.zh: 將軍以龍虎之威，可為之韓、彭邪！

translations.literal: With the General's dragon-tiger might, could you become his Han Xin or Peng Yue!
translations.idiomatic: With your own dragon-and-tiger prowess, would you settle for being his Han Xin or Peng Yue?

sentences.zh: 今兗州雖殘，尚有三城，能戰之士，不下萬人，以將軍之神武，與文若、昱等收而用之，霸王之業可成也，願將軍更慮之！

translations.literal: Though Yan Province is now ravaged, three cities still remain; fighting troops are no fewer than ten thousand. With the General's divine martial prowess, and with Xun Yu, Yu, and the rest gathering and employing them—the work of a hegemon-king can be achieved. I hope the General will reconsider!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Province may be in ruins, but three cities still hold, and more than ten thousand seasoned fighters remain. With your own prowess—and Xun Yu, myself, and the others to rally them—a hegemon's foundation can still be laid. Think again, General!

sentences.zh: 」操乃止。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: "Cao Cao changed his mind.

sentences.zh: 18十二月，司徒淳于嘉罷，以衛尉趙溫為司徒，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: 18 In the twelfth month, Minister over the Masses Chunyu Jia was dismissed; Guard Commandant Zhao Wen was made Minister over the Masses and put in charge of affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Chunyu Jia was dismissed as Minister over the Masses; Zhao Wen, Guard Commandant, was appointed in his place with oversight of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 19馬騰之攻李傕也，劉焉二子範、誕皆死。

translations.literal: 19 When Ma Teng attacked Li Jue, both of Liu Yan's sons Fan and Dan died.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Teng attacked Li Jue, Liu Yan's two sons Fan and Dan both perished.

sentences.zh: 議郎河南龐羲，素與焉善，乃募將焉諸孫入蜀。

translations.literal: Gentleman Consultant Pang Xi of Henan, who had long been on good terms with Yan, thereupon recruited Yan's various grandsons to enter Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xi of Henan, a Gentleman Consultant who had long been close to Liu Yan, then recruited Yan's grandsons to come into Shu.

sentences.zh: 會天火燒城，焉徙治成都，疽發背而卒。

translations.literal: Just then heaven's fire burned the city; Yan moved his seat of government to Chengdu; a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: A fire from heaven burned the capital; Yan relocated his seat of government to Chengdu, but a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.

sentences.zh: 州大吏趙韙等貪焉子璋溫仁，共上璋為益州刺史，詔拜潁川扈瑁為刺史。

translations.literal: Chief clerks of the province such as Zhao Wei and others, coveting Yan's son Zhang's gentle disposition, together recommended Zhang as Inspector of Yi Province; an edict appointed Hu Mao of Yingchuan as Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Senior provincial officials led by Zhao Wei, taken with Liu Zhang's mild and benevolent character, jointly recommended him as Inspector of Yi Province—but the court appointed Hu Mao of Yingchuan instead.

sentences.zh: 璋將沈彌、婁發、甘寧反，擊璋，不勝，走入荊州；

translations.literal: Zhang's generals Shen Mi, Lou Fa, and Gan Ning rebelled, attacked Zhang, did not prevail, and fled into Jing Province;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang's officers Shen Mi, Lou Fa, and Gan Ning rose in revolt against him, were defeated, and fled into Jing Province;

sentences.zh: 詔乃以璋為益州牧。

translations.literal: an edict thereupon appointed Zhang as Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: whereupon an edict confirmed Liu Zhang as Governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 璋以韙為征東中郎將，率眾擊劉表，屯朐*[月忍]*。

translations.literal: Zhang appointed Wei as General of the Household Who Conquers the East, leading troops to attack Liu Biao, encamped at Qurén.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang made Zhao Wei General of the Household Who Conquers the East and sent him against Liu Biao, camped at Qurén.

sentences.zh: 20徐州牧陶謙疾篤，謂別駕東海麋竺曰：「非劉備不能安此州也。

translations.literal: 20 Governor of Xu Province Tao Qian was gravely ill; he said to his Chancellor of the Separate Office Mi Zhu of Donghai: "Without Liu Bei this province cannot be secured.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tao Qian of Xu Province lay gravely ill. He told his Chancellor Mi Zhu of Donghai, "Only Liu Bei can hold this province.

sentences.zh: 」謙卒，竺率州人迎備。

translations.literal: " When Qian died, Zhu led the people of the province to welcome Bei.
translations.idiomatic: "When Qian died, Mi Zhu rallied the province to receive Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 備未敢當，曰：「袁公路近在壽春，〔此君四世五公，海內所歸〕<ref>〔此君四世五公海內所歸〕據《三國志．先主傳》增補，以對正後文「塚中枯骨，何足介意」。

translations.literal: Bei did not dare accept and said: "Yuan Gonglu is near at Shouchun—[this lord is of four generations and five high offices, to whom all within the seas turn]<ref>[This lord is of four generations and five high offices, to whom all within the seas turn] Supplemented according to the Biography of the Founding Emperor in Records of the Three Kingdoms, to correspond with the later phrase "bones in a tomb, why bother to mind them."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei hesitated to accept and said, "Yuan Shu of Shouchun is close at hand—[four generations, five marquisates—all within the seas look to him]<ref>[Four generations, five marquisates—all within the seas look to him] Added from the Biography of the Founding Emperor in Records of the Three Kingdoms to align with the later line "bones in a tomb—why bother?"

sentences.zh: </ref>，君可以州與之。

translations.literal: </ref>; you may give the province to him.
translations.idiomatic: Give the province to him instead.

sentences.zh: 」典農校尉下邳陳登曰：「公路驕豪，非治亂之主。

translations.literal: " Agricultural Commandant Chen Deng of Xiapi said: "Gonglu is proud and overbearing—not a ruler for times of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: "Chen Deng, Agricultural Commandant of Xiapi, replied, "Yuan Shu is arrogant and violent—not a man to restore order.

sentences.zh: 今欲為使君合步騎十萬，上可以匡主濟民，下可以割地守境；

translations.literal: Now I wish to assemble for you, my lord, a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry; above you can support the sovereign and succor the people, below you can hold territory and guard the borders;
translations.idiomatic: "Let me raise a hundred thousand foot and horse for you, my lord—enough to aid the throne and the people from above, and to hold your own ground below;

sentences.zh: 若使君不見聽許，登亦未敢聽使君也。

translations.literal: if you, my lord, will not heed and consent, then Deng also dares not obey you, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse, then I cannot follow you either.

sentences.zh: 」北海相孔融謂備曰：「袁公路豈憂國忘家者邪！

translations.literal: " Chancellor of Beihai Kong Rong said to Bei: "Is Yuan Gonglu one who forgets his country for his family!
translations.idiomatic: "Kong Rong, Chancellor of Beihai, told Liu Bei, "Since when is Yuan Shu a patriot!

sentences.zh: 塚中枯骨，何足介意！

translations.literal: Bones in a tomb—why bother to mind them!
translations.idiomatic: Bones in a tomb—why should you care about them!

sentences.zh: 今日之事，百姓與能。

translations.literal: In today's affair, it is the people and the worthy who matter.
translations.idiomatic: What matters today is the will of the people and the worthiness of the man.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，悔不可追。

translations.literal: Heaven gives and you do not take—regret cannot be undone.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven offers and you refuse—you will regret it forever.

sentences.zh: 」備遂領徐州。

translations.literal: " Bei thereupon took charge of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: "Liu Bei accepted and assumed command of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 21初，太傅馬日磾與趙岐俱奉使至壽春，岐守志不橈，袁術憚之。

translations.literal: 21 Earlier, Grand Tutor Ma Midi and Zhao Qi were both sent as envoys to Shouchun; Qi held to his integrity and would not bend, and Yuan Shu feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Grand Tutor Ma Midi and Zhao Qi had both been sent as envoys to Shouchun. Zhao Qi stood firm and would not yield, and Yuan Shu feared him.

sentences.zh: 日磾頗有求於術。

translations.literal: Midi had made considerable requests of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Midi, by contrast, had curried favor with Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 術侵侮之，從日磾借節視之，因奪不還，條軍中十餘人，使促辟之。

translations.literal: Shu insulted and humiliated him, borrowed Midi's staff of office to examine it, then seized it and would not return it; he listed more than ten men in the army and had them urgently summon him to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu bullied him, borrowed and inspected his credential of office, then seized it and refused to return it. He named more than ten officers and ordered them to press Ma Midi into service.

sentences.zh: 日磾從術求去，術留不遣，又欲逼為軍師。

translations.literal: Midi sought leave from Shu to depart; Shu detained him and would not release him, and also wished to force him to become military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Midi asked leave to depart; Yuan Shu kept him and also tried to appoint him military adviser.

sentences.zh: 日磾病其失節，嘔血而死。

translations.literal: Midi was pained at the loss of integrity and vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: Disgraced at the loss of his integrity, Ma Midi spat blood and died.

sentences.zh: 22初，孫堅娶錢唐吳氏，生四男策、權、翊、匡及一女。

translations.literal: 22 Earlier, Sun Jian took to wife the Lady Wu of Qiantang and had four sons—Ce, Quan, Yi, and Kuang—and one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian had married Lady Wu of Qiantang, who bore him four sons—Ce, Quan, Yi, and Kuang—and one daughter.

sentences.zh: 堅從軍於外，留家壽春。

translations.literal: Jian followed the army abroad and left his family at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Jian served on distant campaigns and left his family at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 策年十餘歲，已交結知名。

translations.literal: Ce was a little more than ten years old and had already formed acquaintance with celebrated men.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce was barely in his teens and had already befriended notable men.

sentences.zh: 舒人周瑜與策同年，亦英達夙成。

translations.literal: Zhou Yu of Shu was the same age as Ce and was also outstandingly gifted from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu of Shu, the same age as Sun Ce, was likewise precocious and gifted.

sentences.zh: 聞策聲問，自舒來造焉，便推結分好，勸策徙居舒；

translations.literal: Hearing of Ce's reputation, he came from Shu to visit him; on the spot they pledged friendship and urged Ce to move his residence to Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Sun Ce's name, Zhou Yu traveled from Shu to meet him. The two bonded at once; Zhou Yu urged Ce to move his household to Shu;

sentences.zh: 策從之。

translations.literal: Ce followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce agreed.

sentences.zh: 瑜乃推道南大宅與策，升堂拜母，有無通共。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon offered his great mansion south of the road to Ce; they entered the hall and bowed to each other's mothers; in having and not having they shared in common.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu gave Sun Ce his fine mansion on the south side of the road. They entered the hall and bowed to each other's mothers, sharing everything they had.

sentences.zh: 及堅死，策年十七，還葬曲阿；

translations.literal: When Jian died, Ce was seventeen; he returned to bury him at Qu'e;
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian died, Sun Ce was seventeen. He returned to bury his father at Qu'e;

sentences.zh: 已乃渡江，居江都，結納豪俊，有復仇之志。

translations.literal: then he crossed the river, resided at Jiangdu, gathered bold heroes, and had the ambition to avenge.
translations.idiomatic: then he crossed the Yangtze, settled at Jiangdu, rallied bold men, and nursed a vow of vengeance.

sentences.zh: 丹陽太守會稽周昕與袁術相惡，術上策舅吳景領丹陽太守，攻昕，奪其郡，以策從兄賁為丹陽都尉。

translations.literal: Administrator of Danyang Zhou Xin of Kuaiji was on bad terms with Yuan Shu; Shu had Ce's maternal uncle Wu Jing take charge as Administrator of Danyang, attacked Xin, seized his commandery, and made Ce's cousin Ben Danyang Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xin, Administrator of Danyang in Kuaiji, was at odds with Yuan Shu. Shu installed Sun Ce's uncle Wu Jing as Administrator of Danyang; they attacked Xin, seized the commandery, and made Ce's cousin Sun Ben Commandant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 策以母弟託廣陵張紘，逕到壽春見袁術。

translations.literal: Ce entrusted his mother and younger brother to Zhang Hong of Guangling and went straight to Shouchun to see Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce left his mother and younger brother in Zhang Hong's care in Guangling and went straight to Shouchun to see Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 涕泣言曰：「亡父昔從長沙入討董卓，與明使君會於南陽，同盟結好，不幸遇難，勳業不終。

translations.literal: Weeping he spoke and said: "My late father formerly followed from Changsha in the campaign against Dong Zhuo; he met with Your Illustrious Lordship at Nanyang, formed alliance and friendship, but unluckily met disaster; his meritorious enterprise was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: In tears he said, "My dead father marched from Changsha against Dong Zhuo and met Your Illustrious Lordship at Nanyang. You swore alliance and friendship—but disaster struck, and his great work was left unfinished.

sentences.zh: 策感惟先人舊恩，欲自憑結，願明使君垂察其城！

translations.literal: Ce is moved by thinking of my forebear's old kindness and wishes to attach myself by my own effort; I hope Your Illustrious Lordship will extend your scrutiny to my sincerity!
translations.idiomatic: Moved by my father's old bond with you, I come seeking your patronage—I beg you to look upon me with sincere regard!

sentences.zh: 」術甚奇之，然未肯還其父兵，謂策曰：「孤用貴舅為丹陽太守，賢從伯陽為都尉，彼精兵之地，可還依召募。

translations.literal: " Shu thought him very extraordinary but was not yet willing to return his father's troops; he said to Ce: "I employ your honored maternal uncle as Administrator of Danyang and your worthy elder cousin Boyang as Commandant—that is a land of picked troops; you may return and rely on them to recruit.
translations.idiomatic: "Yuan Shu was greatly impressed but would not yet return his father's troops. He told Sun Ce, "I have placed your uncle Wu Jing in Danyang and your cousin Sun Ben as commandant—that is prime recruiting country. Go back and raise men there.

sentences.zh: 」策遂與汝南呂範及族人孫河迎其母詣曲阿，依舅氏。

translations.literal: " Ce thereupon together with Lü Fan of Runan and his clansman Sun He went to meet his mother at Qu'e and relied on his maternal uncle's household.
translations.idiomatic: "Sun Ce went with Lü Fan of Runan and his kinsman Sun He to fetch his mother to Qu'e and stayed with his uncle's household.

sentences.zh: 因緣召募，得數百人，而為涇縣大帥祖郎所襲，幾至危殆。

translations.literal: Taking the opportunity he recruited and obtained several hundred men; but the great chief Zu Lang of Jing county attacked him and he almost reached peril.
translations.idiomatic: He began recruiting and gathered several hundred men, but Zu Lang, a bandit chief of Jing county, ambushed him and nearly killed him.

sentences.zh: 於是復往見術。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again went to see Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Yuan Shu again.

sentences.zh: 術以堅餘兵千餘人還策，表拜懷義校尉。

translations.literal: Shu returned to Ce more than a thousand of Jian's remaining troops and recommended him as Colonel Who Cherishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu restored more than a thousand of Sun Jian's old soldiers to Sun Ce and recommended him as Colonel Who Cherishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 策騎士有罪，逃入術營，隱於內廄。

translations.literal: A cavalryman of Ce committed a crime, fled into Shu's camp, and hid in the inner stable.
translations.idiomatic: One of Sun Ce's horsemen committed a crime, fled into Yuan Shu's camp, and hid in the stable.

sentences.zh: 策指使人就斬之，訖，詣術謝。

translations.literal: Ce sent someone to go and behead him; when it was finished, he went to Shu to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce sent men to cut him down, then went to Yuan Shu to apologize.

sentences.zh: 術曰：「兵人好叛，當共疾之，何為謝也！

translations.literal: Shu said: "Soldiers are prone to desertion; we should together hate this—why apologize!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu said, "Soldiers desert—we should hate it together. Why apologize?

sentences.zh: 」由是軍中益畏憚之。

translations.literal: " From this the army feared and respected him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: "From that moment his troops feared him all the more.

sentences.zh: 術初許以策為九江太守，已而更用丹陽陳紀。

translations.literal: Shu at first promised to make Ce Administrator of Jiujiang, but then replaced him with Chen Ji of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu had first promised Sun Ce the post of Administrator of Jiujiang, then gave it to Chen Ji of Danyang instead.

sentences.zh: 後術欲攻徐州，從廬江太守陸康求米三萬斛；

translations.literal: Later Shu wished to attack Xu Province and requested thirty thousand hu of grain from Lu Kang, Administrator of Lujiang;
translations.idiomatic: Later, planning an attack on Xu Province, Yuan Shu asked Lu Kang, Administrator of Lujiang, for thirty thousand bushels of grain;

sentences.zh: 康不與。

translations.literal: Kang would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang refused.

sentences.zh: 術大怒，遣策攻康，謂曰：「前錯用陳紀，每恨本意不遂。

translations.literal: Shu was greatly angered and sent Ce to attack Kang, saying to him: "Previously I wrongly used Chen Ji; each time I regret that my original intention was not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Yuan Shu sent Sun Ce against Lu Kang and told him, "I misused Chen Ji before—that still rankles.

sentences.zh: 今若得康，廬江真卿有也。

translations.literal: If now we can take Kang, Lujiang will truly be yours.
translations.idiomatic: Take Lu Kang, and Lujiang is truly yours.

sentences.zh: 」策攻康，拔之，術復用其故吏劉勳為太守；

translations.literal: " Ce attacked Kang, captured it; Shu again used his former subordinate Liu Xun as Administrator;
translations.idiomatic: "Sun Ce captured Lu Kang—but Yuan Shu installed his old officer Liu Xun as administrator instead;

sentences.zh: 策益失望。

translations.literal: Ce grew all the more disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce's disillusion grew.

sentences.zh: 侍御史劉繇，岱之弟也，素有盛名，詔書用為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Liu Yao, younger brother of Dai, had long had a famous reputation; an edict employed him as Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Liu Yao, younger brother of Liu Dai, was already renowned; the court appointed him Inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 州舊治壽春，術已據之，繇欲南渡江，吳景、孫賁迎置曲阿。

translations.literal: The province's former seat was Shouchun; Shu had already occupied it; Yao wished to cross south over the river; Wu Jing and Sun Ben welcomed and installed him at Qu'e.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial capital had been Shouchun, now held by Yuan Shu. Liu Yao planned to cross the Yangtze; Wu Jing and Sun Ben received him and established him at Qu'e.

sentences.zh: 及策攻廬江，繇聞之，以景、賁本術所置，懼為袁、孫所併，遂構嫌隙，迫逐景、賁。

translations.literal: When Ce attacked Lujiang, Yao heard of it; because Jing and Ben had originally been placed by Shu, he feared being swallowed by Yuan and Sun together; thereupon he fostered suspicion and discord and drove away Jing and Ben.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce attacked Lujiang, Liu Yao learned that Wu Jing and Sun Ben had been Yuan Shu's appointees. Fearing annexation by Yuan Shu and Sun Ce together, he turned hostile and drove them out.

sentences.zh: 景、賁退屯歷陽。

translations.literal: Jing and Ben withdrew and encamped at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing and Sun Ben withdrew to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 繇遣將樊能、于糜屯橫江，張英屯當利口以拒之。

translations.literal: Yao sent his generals Fan Neng and Yu Mi to encamp at Hengjiang, and Zhang Ying to encamp at Danglikou to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao posted Fan Neng and Yu Mi at Hengjiang and Zhang Ying at Danglikou to block them.

sentences.zh: 術乃自用故吏惠衢為揚州刺史，以景為督軍中郎將，與賁共將兵擊英等。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon himself employed his former subordinate Hui Qu as Inspector of Yang Province, made Jing General Who Oversees the Army, and together with Ben led troops to attack Ying and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu named his old officer Hui Qu Inspector of Yang Province, made Wu Jing General Who Oversees the Army, and sent him with Sun Ben against Zhang Ying and the others.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，癸丑，赦天下。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on the day guichou, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on guichou day, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 2曹操敗呂布於定陶。

translations.literal: 2 Cao Cao defeated Lü Bu at Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao defeated Lü Bu at Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 3詔即拜袁紹為右將軍。

translations.literal: 3 An edict immediately appointed Yuan Shao as General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Yuan Shao was at once appointed General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 4董卓初死，三輔民尚數十萬戶，李傕等放兵劫略，加以饑饉，二年間，民相食略盡。

translations.literal: 4 When Dong Zhuo had just died, the people of the Three Adjuncts still numbered several hundred thousand households; Li Jue and the others let troops loose to plunder and rob; added to this was famine; within two years the people eating one another were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After Dong Zhuo's death the Three Adjuncts still held several hundred thousand households. Li Jue and his faction unleashed their troops to plunder, and famine followed. Within two years cannibalism had nearly wiped the populace out.

sentences.zh: 李傕、郭汜、樊稠各相與矜功爭權，欲鬥者數矣，賈詡每以大體責之，雖內不能善，外相含容。

translations.literal: Li Jue, Guo Si, and Fan Chou each mutually prided themselves on merit and struggled for power; times when they wished to fight were several; Jia Xu each time rebuked them with reference to the greater scheme; although inwardly they could not be harmonious, outwardly they mutually tolerated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue, Guo Si, and Fan Chou each vaunted his own achievements and wrestled for power; more than once they nearly came to blows. Jia Xu repeatedly rebuked them in the name of the greater interest. Though they could not truly reconcile, they maintained an outward show of forbearance.

sentences.zh: 樊稠之擊馬騰、韓遂也，李利戰不甚力，稠叱之曰：「人欲截汝父頭，何敢如此！

translations.literal: When Fan Chou attacked Ma Teng and Han Sui, Li Li did not fight with much force; Chou scolded him and said: "People wish to cut off your father's head—how dare you act thus!
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Chou fought Ma Teng and Han Sui, his nephew Li Li held back in battle. Fan Chou berated him: "They mean to cut off your father's head—and you fight like this?

sentences.zh: 我不能斬卿邪！

translations.literal: Can I not behead you!
translations.idiomatic: Do you think I cannot strike off your head?

sentences.zh: 」及騰、遂敗走，稠追至陳倉，遂語稠曰：「本所爭者非私怨，王家事耳。

translations.literal: " When Teng and Sui were defeated and fled, Chou pursued to Chencang; Sui spoke to Chou and said: "What we originally contended over was not personal grudge—it was the royal house's affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Teng and Han Sui broke and fled, Fan Chou pursued them to Chencang. Han Sui said to him: "Our quarrel was never personal—it was service to the throne.

sentences.zh: 與足下州里人，欲相與善語而別。

translations.literal: You and I are men of the same province and district; I wish to exchange good words and part.
translations.idiomatic: We are countrymen. Let us speak as friends and part.

sentences.zh: 」乃俱卻騎，前接馬，交臂相加，共語良久而別。

translations.literal: " Thereupon both reined back their horses, went forward and met horses, linked arms, spoke together at length, and parted.
translations.idiomatic: Both men reined in, rode forward, met hand to hand, and clasped arms. They talked at length before going their separate ways.

sentences.zh: 軍還，李利告傕：「韓、樊交馬語，不知所道，意愛甚密。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Li Li told Jue: "Han and Fan met horses and spoke; one does not know what they said; their affection seemed very close.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return Li Li reported to Li Jue: "Han Sui and Fan Chou met and spoke face to face—I cannot say what passed between them, but they seemed on the closest terms.

sentences.zh: 」傕亦以稠勇而得眾，忌之。

translations.literal: " Jue also because Chou was brave and gained the masses' support, was jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue, for his part, envied Fan Chou's bravery and the loyalty of his troops.

sentences.zh: 稠欲將兵東出關，從傕索益兵。

translations.literal: Chou wished to lead troops east out of the pass and requested additional troops from Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chou wanted to lead his forces east out of the pass and asked Li Jue for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 二月，傕請稠會議，便於坐殺稠。

translations.literal: In the second month, Jue invited Chou to a council meeting and killed him right in his seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Jue invited Fan Chou to a council and had him slain on the spot.

sentences.zh: 由是諸將轉相疑貳。

translations.literal: From this the generals in turn mutually grew suspicious and divided.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the generals grew mutually suspicious and began to divide among themselves.

sentences.zh: 傕數設酒請郭汜，或留汜止宿。

translations.literal: Jue repeatedly set out wine to invite Guo Si, sometimes keeping Si to stay the night.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue repeatedly feasted Guo Si and sometimes kept him overnight.

sentences.zh: 汜妻恐汜愛傕婢妾，思有以間之。

translations.literal: Si's wife feared Si would come to love Jue's maidservants and concubines and thought of a way to drive a wedge between them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si's wife feared he might grow fond of Li Jue's maids and concubines, and looked for a way to turn them against each other.

sentences.zh: 會傕送饋，妻以豉為藥，擿以示汜曰：「一棲不兩雄，我固疑將軍信李公也。

translations.literal: It happened that Jue sent food gifts; the wife took fermented beans as poison, picked them out and showed Si and said: "One nest does not hold two males—I have long suspected the General trusts Lord Li.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jue sent a gift of food, she picked out the fermented beans, showed them to Guo Si, and said: "Two roosters cannot share one perch—I have long suspected you are too close to Li Jue.

sentences.zh: 」他日，傕復請汜，飲大醉，汜疑其有毒，絞糞汁飲之，於是各治兵相攻矣。

translations.literal: " Another day Jue again invited Si; drinking he became very drunk; Si suspected there was poison and squeezed dung juice to drink; thereupon each mustered troops and attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion Li Jue invited him again. Guo Si drank himself insensible, then fearing poison forced down a draught of strained dung-water as an antidote. After that both sides mobilized for war.

sentences.zh: 帝使侍中、尚書和傕、汜，傕、汜不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Palace Attendants and Masters of Writing to reconcile Jue and Si; Jue and Si would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Palace Attendants and Masters of Writing to mediate between Li Jue and Guo Si; neither would listen.

sentences.zh: 汜謀迎帝幸其營，夜有亡者。

translations.literal: Si plotted to welcome the Emperor to favor his camp; at night there was a deserter.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si plotted to bring the emperor to his camp. That night someone deserted.

sentences.zh: 告傕。

translations.literal: He reported to Jue.
translations.idiomatic: The deserter informed Li Jue.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙寅，傕使兄子暹將數千兵圍宮，以車三乘迎帝。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingyin day, Jue sent his elder brother's son Xian to lead several thousand troops to surround the palace; with three carriages he welcomed the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingyin day, Li Jue sent his nephew Li Xian with several thousand troops to surround the palace and escort the emperor away in three carriages.

sentences.zh: 太尉楊彪曰：「自古帝王無在人家者，諸君舉事，奈何如是！

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yang Biao said: "From antiquity emperors and kings have none who dwell in others' households; you gentlemen raise affairs—how can it be thus!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yang Biao protested: "Never in history has an emperor lived as a guest in another man's house. Gentlemen, is this how you conduct your affairs?

sentences.zh: 」暹曰：「將軍計定矣。

translations.literal: " Xian said: "The General's plan is settled.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xian replied, "My uncle's decision stands.

sentences.zh: 」於是君臣步從乘輿以出，兵即入殿中，掠宮人、御物。

translations.literal: " Thereupon lord and ministers on foot followed the imperial carriage to go out; troops immediately entered the hall and plundered palace women and imperial goods.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor and court then walked out behind the imperial carriage. Li Jue's troops at once entered the palace halls and looted the women of the harem and the imperial stores.

sentences.zh: 帝至傕營，傕又徙御府金帛置其營，遂放火燒宮殿、官府、民居悉盡。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Jue's camp, Jue again moved the imperial treasury's gold and silk to place in his camp; thereupon he set fire and burned palaces, government offices, and common dwellings—all to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Li Jue's camp, Li Jue moved the imperial gold and silk into his own quarters, then set fire and burned the palaces, government offices, and private dwellings to ash.

sentences.zh: 帝復使公卿和傕、汜，汜留楊彪及司空張喜、尚書王隆、光祿勳劉淵、衛尉士孫瑞、太僕韓融、廷尉宣璠、大鴻臚榮郃、大司農朱儁、將作大匠梁邵、屯騎校尉姜宣等於其營為質。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent the Ducal Ministers to reconcile Jue and Si; Si detained Yang Biao and Minister of Works Zhang Xi, Master of Writing Wang Long, Director of Retainers Liu Yuan, Commandant of the Guards Sun Rui, Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud Han Rong, Commandant of Justice Xuan Fan, Grand Herald Rong He, Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhu Jun, Master of Craftsmen Liang Shao, Commandant of the Warden of the Cavaliers Jiang Xuan, and others at his camp as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent the chief ministers to mediate. Guo Si kept Yang Biao, Zhang Xi, Wang Long, Liu Yuan, Sun Rui, Han Rong, Xuan Fan, Rong He, Zhu Jun, Liang Shao, Jiang Xuan, and others as hostages in his camp.

sentences.zh: 朱儁憤懣發病死。

translations.literal: Zhu Jun, in indignant vexation, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jun died of illness brought on by rage and grief.

translations.literal: In this year the fourth month begins on renshen; there is no jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: In this year the fourth month begins on renshen; there is no jiazi day.

translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Xian in the Book of Later Han and the Annals of Later Han both read jiawu, the twenty-third day of the month; the text is amended accordingly.
