translations.literal: </ref>; the Honored Lady of the Fu clan of Langya was established as Empress;
translations.idiomatic: —the Honored Lady Fu of Langya was made empress;

sentences.zh: 以后父侍中完為執金吾。

translations.literal: the empress's father, Palace Attendant Wan, was made Bearer of the Mace.
translations.idiomatic: and her father, Palace Attendant Fu Wan, was appointed Bearer of the Mace.

sentences.zh: 6郭汜饗公卿，議政李傕。

translations.literal: 6 Guo Si feasted the Ducal Ministers and deliberated on attacking Li Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si entertained the chief ministers and debated policy against Li Jue.

sentences.zh: 楊彪曰：「群臣共鬥，一人劫天子，一人質公卿，可行乎！

translations.literal: Yang Biao said: "Ministers together fight; one man holds the Son of Heaven hostage, one man holds the Ducal Ministers hostage—can this be done!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao said: "The court is torn by feuding ministers—one faction holds the emperor hostage, another holds the chief ministers hostage. How can this continue?

sentences.zh: 」汜怒，欲手刃之。

translations.literal: " Si grew angry and wished to kill him with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si flew into a rage and meant to cut him down where he stood.

sentences.zh: 彪曰：「卿尚不奉國家，吾豈求生邪！

translations.literal: Biao said: "You still do not serve the state—I, how could I seek to live!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao answered: "If you will not serve the realm, do you think I care to save my own life?

sentences.zh: 」中郎將楊密固諫，汜乃止。

translations.literal: " Palace Gentleman Yang Mi firmly remonstrated; Si then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gentleman Yang Mi interposed firmly, and Guo Si stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 傕召羌、胡數千人，先以御物繒絲采與之，許以宮人、婦女，欲令攻郭汜。

translations.literal: Jue summoned several thousand Qiang and Hu; first gave them imperial goods—silks and colored fabrics—and promised palace women and wives, wishing to make them attack Guo Si.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue called up several thousand Qiang and Hu warriors, paid them with imperial silks and brocades, and promised palace women as reward if they would attack Guo Si.

sentences.zh: 汜陰與傕黨中郎將張苞等謀攻傕。

translations.literal: Si secretly together with Jue's faction's Palace Gentleman Zhang Bao and others plotted to attack Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si secretly plotted with Zhang Bao and other officers of Li Jue's faction to strike Li Jue.

sentences.zh: 丙申，汜將兵夜攻傕門，矢及帝簾帷中，又貫傕左耳。

translations.literal: On bingchen day Si led troops by night to attack Jue's gate; arrows reached the Emperor's curtain and canopy, and also pierced Jue's left ear.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Guo Si attacked Li Jue's gates by night. Arrows flew into the emperor's pavilion; one pierced Li Jue's left ear.

sentences.zh: 苞等燒屋，火不然。

translations.literal: Bao and the others burned houses; the fire would not catch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bao and his men tried to burn the buildings, but the fires would not take.

sentences.zh: 楊奉於外拒汜，汜兵退，苞等因將所領兵歸汜。

translations.literal: Yang Feng at the outside resisted Si; Si's troops withdrew; Bao and the others thereupon led the troops they commanded and returned to Si.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng held Guo Si off from outside. Guo Si's force fell back, and Zhang Bao and his men took their troops over to Guo Si's side.

sentences.zh: 是日，傕復移乘輿境北塢，使校尉監塢門，內外隔絕，侍臣皆有飢色。

translations.literal: That day Jue again moved the imperial carriage to the northern rampart within the territory; he sent a Commandant to monitor the rampart gate; inside and outside were cut off from each other; attendant ministers all had the look of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Li Jue moved the imperial carriage to a fortified compound north of the capital, posted guards at its gate, and cut the court off from the outside world. The attendants were hollow-cheeked with hunger.

sentences.zh: 帝求米五斗、牛骨五具以賜左右。

translations.literal: The Emperor requested five dou of rice and five sets of ox bones to bestow on those around him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked for five pecks of grain and five sets of ox bones to give his attendants.

sentences.zh: 傕曰：「朝晡上飯，何用米為？

translations.literal: Jue said: "Morning and evening rice is served—what use is grain?
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue replied: "You get meals morning and evening—what do you need grain for?

sentences.zh: 」乃以臭牛骨與之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he gave them stinking ox bones.
translations.idiomatic: He sent them rotting ox bones instead.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，欲詰責之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angry and wished to reprove and blame him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and meant to denounce him openly.

sentences.zh: 侍中楊琦諫曰：「傕自知所犯悖逆，欲轉車駕幸池陽黃白城，臣願陛下忍之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yang Qi remonstrated and said: "Jue himself knows the rebellious crime he has committed; he wishes to transfer the imperial carriage to favor Chi Yang's Huangbai City; I hope Your Majesty will endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yang Qi urged restraint: "Li Jue knows he has crossed every line. He may yet move the court to Huangbai City in Chiyang. Your Majesty, I beg you to bear with this for now.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 司徒趙溫與傕書曰：「公前屠陷王城，殺戮大臣，今爭睚眥之隙，以成千鈞之仇。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Zhao Wen wrote to Jue and said: "Sir, you formerly slaughtered and overthrew the royal city, killed and executed great ministers; now over the gap of an eyelash you make a feud of a thousand jun.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Zhao Wen wrote Li Jue: "You sacked the capital and butchered the great ministers. Now you nurse a trifling grudge into a feud that threatens the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲令和解，詔命不行，而復欲轉乘輿於黃白城，此誠老夫所不解也。

translations.literal: The court wishes to make you reconcile; edicts and commands are not obeyed, yet you again wish to transfer the imperial carriage to Huangbai City—this is truly what this old man does not understand.
translations.idiomatic: The court has ordered reconciliation, yet your edicts go unheeded and you would move the emperor again to Huangbai City. An old man like me cannot fathom it.

sentences.zh: 於《易》，一為過，再為涉，三而弗改，滅其頂，凶。

translations.literal: In the Changes: one time is transgression; a second time is wading in; a third time without change—destroyed at the top—misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: the first offense is a mistake, the second a transgression, the third unrepented brings ruin upon the head—misfortune.

sentences.zh: 不如早共和解。

translations.literal: It would be better early to mutually harmonize and dissolve.
translations.idiomatic: Reconcile now, while you still can.

sentences.zh: 」傕大怒，欲殺溫，其弟應諫之，數日乃止。

translations.literal: " Jue was greatly angry and wished to kill Wen; his younger brother Ying remonstrated with him; after several days he then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue raged and wanted Zhao Wen killed. His brother dissuaded him, and after several days Li Jue relented.

sentences.zh: 傕信巫覡厭勝之術，常以三牲祠董卓於省門外。

translations.literal: Jue trusted wizards' and shamans' arts of overcoming by suppression; he constantly used the three sacrificial animals to sacrifice to Dong Zhuo outside the provincial gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue put his faith in sorcery and regularly offered the three sacrificial beasts to Dong Zhuo outside the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 每對帝或言「明陛下」，或言「明帝」，為帝說郭汜無狀，帝亦隨其意應答之。

translations.literal: Each time facing the Emperor he sometimes said "Illustrious Your Majesty," sometimes said "Illustrious Emperor;" he spoke to the Emperor of Guo Si's disorderly conduct; the Emperor also followed his intent in responding.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke with the emperor he addressed him as "Your Illustrious Majesty" or "Illustrious Emperor," vilified Guo Si, and the emperor answered as Li Jue wished.

sentences.zh: 傕喜，自謂良得天子歡心也。

translations.literal: Jue was pleased and considered that he had truly won the Son of Heaven's delighted heart.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue was pleased, believing he had truly won the emperor's affection.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己卯，帝使竭者僕射皇甫酈和傕、汜。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on jimao day, the Emperor sent the Bearer of the Staff Huangfu Li to reconcile Jue and Si.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jimao day, the emperor sent Bearer of the Staff Huangfu Li to mediate between Li Jue and Guo Si.

sentences.zh: 酈先詣汜，汜從命；

translations.literal: Li first went to Si; Si obeyed the command;
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Li went first to Guo Si, who agreed to negotiate;

sentences.zh: 又詣人鶴，傕不肯，曰：「郭多，盜馬虜耳，何敢欲與吾等邪！

translations.literal: He again went to Li Jue; Jue would not comply and said: "Guo Duo is only a horse-thieving barbarian—how dare he wish to rank with us!
translations.idiomatic: Then he went to Li Jue, who refused and said: "Guo Duo is a mere horse-thieving savage—how dare he presume to stand equal with us!

sentences.zh: 必誅之！

translations.literal: He must be executed!
translations.idiomatic: He must die!

sentences.zh: 君觀吾方略士眾，足辦郭多否邪？

translations.literal: Sir, look at my strategy and troops—are they sufficient to deal with Guo Duo or not?
translations.idiomatic: Look at my forces and my plans—are they not enough to finish off Guo Duo?

sentences.zh: 郭多又劫質公卿，所為如是，而君苟欲左右之邪？

translations.literal: Guo Duo furthermore holds the Ducal Ministers hostage—his conduct is thus—yet you would casually wish to be partial to him!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si holds the chief ministers hostage and behaves as he does—and you would still take his side?

sentences.zh: 」酈曰：「近者董公之強，將軍所知也；

translations.literal: " Li said: "Recently Lord Dong's strength—the General knows of it;
translations.idiomatic: " Huangfu Li replied: "You know yourself how powerful Dong Zhuo once was;

sentences.zh: 呂布受恩而反圖之，斯須之間，身首異處，此有勇而無謀也。

translations.literal: Lü Bu received favor yet turned to plot against him; in the space of a moment, body and head in different places—this is having courage but no strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu owed him everything, then turned on him—in an instant head and body lay apart. Courage without wisdom.

sentences.zh: 今將軍身為上將，荷國寵榮，汜質公卿而將軍脅主，誰輕重乎！

translations.literal: Now the General personally is a chief general, bears the state's favor and glory; Si holds the Ducal Ministers hostage while the General coerces the sovereign—who is lighter and who heavier!
translations.idiomatic: You are the senior general, showered with imperial favor. Guo Si holds the ministers hostage; you hold the emperor. Which of you weighs heavier in guilt?

sentences.zh: 張濟與汜有謀，楊奉，白波賊帥耳，猶知將軍所為非是，將軍雖寵之，猶不為用也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji has conspiracies with Si; Yang Feng is only a White Wave Bandits' chief—yet even they know the General's conduct is wrong; though the General favors them, they still will not be used by you.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji conspires with Guo Si. Yang Feng is only a White Wave bandit chief—yet even he knows what you do is wrong. Favor them as you may, they will not truly serve you.

sentences.zh: 」傕呵之令出。

translations.literal: " Jue shouted at him and ordered him out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue bellowed at him to get out.

sentences.zh: 酈出，詣省門，白「傕不肯奉詔，辭語不順。

translations.literal: Li went out, went to the provincial gate, reported: "Jue will not obey the edict; his words are not compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Li left and at the palace gate reported: "Li Jue refuses the imperial command and speaks defiantly.

sentences.zh: 」帝恐傕聞之，亟令酈去。

translations.literal: " The Emperor feared Jue would hear it and urgently ordered Li to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Li Jue would overhear, the emperor hurried Huangfu Li away.

sentences.zh: 傕遣虎賁王昌呼，欲殺之，昌知酈忠直，縱令去，還答傕，言「追之不及」。

translations.literal: Jue dispatched a tiger guard Wang Chang to summon him, wishing to kill him; Chang knew Li was upright and loyal and let him go; returning he answered Jue, saying "Could not overtake him."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue sent his guard Wang Chang to fetch Huangfu Li and kill him. Wang Chang, knowing Huangfu Li's integrity, let him escape and told Li Jue he could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以車騎將軍李傕為大司馬，在三公之右。

translations.literal: On xinsi day Li Jue, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was made Grand Marshal, to the right of the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day Li Jue, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was appointed Grand Marshal, ranking above the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 7呂布將薛蘭、李封屯巨野，曹操攻之，布救蘭等，不勝而走，操遂斬蘭等。

translations.literal: 7 Lü Bu's generals Xue Lan and Li Feng encamped at Juye; Cao Cao attacked them; Bu rescued Lan and the others but did not prevail and fled; Cao thereupon beheaded Lan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's generals Xue Lan and Li Feng held Juye. Cao Cao attacked; Lü Bu came to their relief but was driven off, and Cao Cao executed Xue Lan and Li Feng.

sentences.zh: 操軍乘氏，以陶謙已死。

translations.literal: Cao's army was at Shengshi; because Tao Qian had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao halted at Shengshi. Tao Qian had died,

sentences.zh: 欲遂取徐州，還乃定布。

translations.literal: He wished forthwith to take Xu Province and return afterward to settle Bu.
translations.idiomatic: and he meant to seize Xu Province at once, then return to finish off Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 荀彧曰：「昔高祖保關中，光武據河內，皆深根固本以制天下，進足以勝敵，退足以堅守，故雖有困敗而終濟大業。

translations.literal: Xun Yu said: "Formerly the High Ancestor preserved Guanzhong, Emperor Guangwu held Henei—both deeply rooted and solidly established themselves to control all under Heaven; advancing was sufficient to overcome the enemy, retreating sufficient to hold firm; thus although there were setbacks and defeats, they finally accomplished the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu said: "The High Ancestor secured Guanzhong; Emperor Guangwu held Henei—each planted deep roots before he mastered the realm. Strong enough to advance and win, secure enough to retreat and hold, they weathered defeat and still achieved the great work.

sentences.zh: 將軍本以兗州首事，平山東之難，百姓無不歸心悅服。

translations.literal: The General originally with Yan Province first raised affairs, pacified the difficulties east of the mountains—the common people none did not turn their hearts and rejoice in submission.
translations.idiomatic: You raised your banner in Yan Province and pacified the lands east of the mountains. The people look to you with loyal hearts.

sentences.zh: 且河、濟，天下之要地也，今雖殘壞，猶易以自保，是亦將軍之關中、河內也，不可以不先定。

translations.literal: Moreover the Yellow River and Ji are the crucial lands of all under Heaven; although now ravaged and ruined, they are still easy by which to preserve oneself—this too is the General's Guanzhong and Henei—it cannot but be settled first.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River and the Ji region are the heartland of the realm. Though wasted now, you can still hold them—they are your Guanzhong and Henei. You must secure them first.

sentences.zh: 今已破李封、薛蘭，若分兵東擊陳宮，宮必不敢西顧，以其間〔勒兵〕收熟麥<ref>以其間〔勒兵〕收熟麥據章注及《魏志．荀彧傳》補。

translations.literal: Now having already broken Li Feng and Xue Lan, if you divide troops east to strike Chen Gong, Gong surely will not dare look west; in that interval [lead the army] to gather ripe wheat<ref>During that interval [lead the army] to gather ripe wheat supplemented according to Zhang's commentary and the Biography of Xun Yu in the Records of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: You have already defeated Li Feng and Xue Lan. Split your forces and strike Chen Gong in the east—he will not dare look west. In the meantime [march your men] to harvest the ripe wheat<ref>During that interval [march your men] to harvest the ripe wheat Added from Zhang's commentary and the Biography of Xun Yu in Records of Wei.

translations.literal: </ref>; ration food and store grain—in one stroke Bu can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: —live on short rations, store grain, and Lü Bu can be crushed in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 破布，然後南結揚州，共討袁術，以臨淮、泗。

translations.literal: Having broken Bu, then south ally with Yang Province, together attack Yuan Shu, to overlook the Huai and Si.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lü Bu is gone, ally with Yang Province to the south, join in attacking Yuan Shu, and press toward the Huai and Si rivers.

sentences.zh: 若捨布而東，多留兵則不足用，少留兵則民皆保城，不得樵采，布乘虛寇暴，民心益危，唯〔鄄〕(

translations.literal: If you abandon Bu and go east, keeping many troops then they are insufficient to use; keeping few troops then the people all will fortify the cities and cannot go out to gather firewood; Bu will seize the void to raid and plunder; the people's hearts will grow more perilous—only [Yan] (
translations.idiomatic: If you leave Lü Bu and march east, a large garrison leaves too few men for the campaign, but a small garrison lets the people flee behind city walls with no one to gather fuel or fodder. Lü Bu will raid at will and the people's loyalty will fail. Only [Yan] (

translations.idiomatic: —the rest would no longer be yours. You would lose Yan Province entirely.

sentences.zh: 若徐州不定，將軍當安所歸乎！

translations.literal: If Xu Province is not settled, where should the General turn to return!
translations.idiomatic: If you fail to take Xu Province, where will you have to go?

sentences.zh: 且陶謙雖死，徐州未易亡也。

translations.literal: Moreover although Tao Qian has died, Xu Province is not easy to destroy.
translations.idiomatic: Even with Tao Qian dead, Xu Province will not fall easily.

sentences.zh: 彼懲往年之敗，將懼而結親，相為表裡。

translations.literal: They will take warning from the defeat of former years; they will fear and form alliances; they will act as outer and inner for each other.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened by your past defeat there, they will fear you and make common cause, backing one another.

sentences.zh: 今東方皆已收表，必堅壁清野以待將軍，攻之不拔，略之無獲，不出十日，則十萬之眾，未戰而先自困耳。

translations.literal: Now the east all have gathered the harvest; they surely will fortify walls and clear the countryside to await the General; attacking they cannot pull out, raiding they obtain nothing; within not ten days, then a hundred thousand masses, before fighting will first weary themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The east has already brought in the harvest. They will empty the countryside and hold their walls against you. Sieges will fail; raids will yield nothing. Within ten days your army of a hundred thousand will collapse from exhaustion before a blow is struck.

sentences.zh: 前討徐州，威罰實行，其子弟念父兄之恥，必人自為守，無降心，就能破之，尚不可有也。

translations.literal: Previously attacking Xu Province, awe and punishment were truly carried out; their sons and younger brothers thinking of their fathers' and elder brothers' shame—surely each man will defend for himself, without a heart to surrender; even if able to break them, still cannot possess them.
translations.idiomatic: Your last campaign in Xu Province was a reign of terror. Sons and brothers remember their fathers' and elder kinsmen's shame. Every man will fight for himself; none will submit. Even if you win, you cannot hold the land.

translations.idiomatic: None of these three courses serves your interest, General. Weigh them carefully.

translations.literal: Bu again came from Dongmin with Chen Gong leading more than ten thousand men to fight; Cao Cao's troops had all gone out to harvest wheat; those present could not reach a thousand; the encampment was not secure.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu marched again from Dongmin with Chen Gong and more than ten thousand men. Cao Cao's soldiers were all out harvesting wheat; fewer than a thousand remained, and the camp was poorly defended.

sentences.zh: 屯西有大堤，其南樹木幽深，操隱兵堤裡，出半兵堤外。

translations.literal: West of the camp was a great embankment; south of it the trees were dense and deep; Cao Cao hid troops inside the embankment and sent half his force outside it.
translations.idiomatic: West of the camp stood a great embankment, with dense woods to the south. Cao Cao hid his men behind the dike and posted half his force in front of it.

sentences.zh: 布夜走，操復攻拔定陶，分兵平諸縣。

translations.literal: Bu fled by night; Cao Cao again attacked and took Dingtao, divided troops to pacify the various counties.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu fled by night. Cao Cao took Dingtao and sent detachments to pacify the surrounding counties.

sentences.zh: 布東奔劉備，張邈從布，使其弟超將家屬保雍兵。

translations.literal: Bu fled east to Liu Bei; Zhang Miao followed Bu and sent his younger brother Chao to lead the family and guard Yong with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu fled east to Liu Bei. Zhang Miao went with him and sent his younger brother Chao to protect the family at Yong with an armed guard.

sentences.zh: 布初見備，甚尊敬之，謂備曰：「我與卿同邊地人也！

translations.literal: When Bu first met Bei, he was very respectful toward him and said to Bei: "You and I are both men of the borderlands!
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Bu first met Liu Bei, he treated him with great respect and said, "You and I are both men of the frontier!

sentences.zh: 布見關東起兵，欲誅董卓。

translations.literal: Bu saw the eastern lords raise troops and wished to execute Dong Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: I saw the lords east of the passes raise armies to destroy Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 布殺卓東出，關東諸將無安布者，皆欲殺布耳。

translations.literal: Bu killed Zhuo and went east; none of the eastern lords would accept Bu—all wished only to kill Bu.
translations.idiomatic: I killed Zhuo and came east, yet not one of those eastern generals would shelter me—they all wanted me dead.

sentences.zh: 」請備於帳中，坐婦床上，令婦向拜，酌酒飲食，名備為弟。

translations.literal: " He invited Bei into his tent, sat on his wife's bed, had his wife bow toward him, poured wine and ate, and called Bei "younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: " He invited Liu Bei into his tent, sat on his wife's bed, had his wife bow to him, poured wine, and shared a meal, calling Liu Bei "younger brother."

sentences.zh: 備見布語言無常，外然之而內不悅。

translations.literal: Bei saw Bu's speech was erratic; outwardly he assented but inwardly was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei found Lü Bu's words unstable and unserious. He agreed outwardly but was displeased within.

sentences.zh: 8李傕、郭汜相攻連月，死者以萬數。

translations.literal: 8 Li Jue and Guo Si attacked each other for months; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Guo Si fought each other for months on end, and the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 六月，傕將楊奉謀殺傕，事泄，遂將兵叛傕，傕眾稍衰。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Li Jue's officer Yang Feng plotted to kill Li Jue; the plot leaked; he thereupon led troops to rebel against Li Jue, and Li Jue's forces gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Yang Feng, an officer under Li Jue, plotted to kill his commander. When the plot leaked, he led his troops in revolt, and Li Jue's strength began to fail.

sentences.zh: 庚午<ref>庚午是年六月庚子朔，無庚午。

translations.literal: On gengwu day<ref>In that year the sixth month opened on gengzi; there was no gengwu day.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day<ref>That year the sixth month opened on gengzi, so there was no gengwu day.

translations.literal: </ref>, General Who Pacifies the East Zhang Ji came from Shaan, wishing to reconcile Li Jue and Guo Si and move the imperial carriage provisionally to Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, Zhang Ji, General Who Pacifies the East, arrived from Shaan intending to reconcile Li Jue and Guo Si and move the imperial carriage temporarily to Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 帝亦思舊京，遣使宣諭，十反，汜、傕許和，欲質其愛子。

translations.literal: The Emperor also missed the old capital; he sent envoys to announce and instruct; ten times back and forth; Guo Si and Li Jue agreed to peace and wished to take each other's beloved sons as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor too longed for the old capital. Envoys went back and forth ten times before Guo Si and Li Jue agreed to peace, each demanding the other's beloved son as hostage.

sentences.zh: 傕妻愛其男，和計未定，而羌、胡數來窺省門，曰：「天子在此中邪！

translations.literal: Li Jue's wife loved her son; the peace plan was undecided, while Qiang and Hu repeatedly came to peer at the palace gates, saying: "Is the Son of Heaven in here?!
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue's wife doted on her son, and the peace plan stalled. Meanwhile Qiang and Hu tribesmen kept peering in at the palace gates, shouting, "Is the Son of Heaven in there?!

sentences.zh: 李將軍許我宮人，今皆何在？

translations.literal: General Li promised us palace women—where are they all now?
translations.idiomatic: General Li promised us palace women—where are they now?

sentences.zh: 」帝患之，使侍中劉艾謂宣義將軍賈詡曰：「卿前奉職公忠，故仍升榮寵；

translations.literal: " The Emperor was troubled by this and sent Palace Attendant Liu Ai to tell General Who Promotes Righteousness Jia Xu: "You formerly served with public loyalty, hence you were still advanced in honor and favor;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was alarmed. He sent Palace Attendant Liu Ai to tell Jia Xu, General Who Promotes Righteousness: "You served the throne with loyal devotion, and for that you were raised to high rank;

sentences.zh: 今羌、胡滿路，宜思方略。

translations.literal: now Qiang and Hu fill the roads—you should think of a strategy."
translations.idiomatic: now Qiang and Hu throng the roads. You must find a way to deal with them."

sentences.zh: 」詡乃召羌、胡大帥飲食之，許以封賞，羌、胡皆引去，傕由此單弱。

translations.literal: " Xu thereupon summoned the Qiang and Hu chieftains to feast them, promised enfeoffments and rewards; the Qiang and Hu all withdrew; Li Jue thereby stood alone and weakened.
translations.idiomatic: " Jia Xu summoned the Qiang and Hu chieftains, feasted them, and promised titles and rewards. They all withdrew, and Li Jue was left isolated and weakened.

sentences.zh: 於是復有言和解之計者，傕乃從之，各以女為質。

translations.literal: Thereupon again some spoke of a plan for reconciliation; Li Jue then complied; each exchanged daughters as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Then others again urged reconciliation. Li Jue agreed, and the two sides exchanged daughters as hostages.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲子<ref>甲子是年七月庚午朔，無甲子。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiazi day<ref>In that year the seventh month opened on gengwu; there was no jiazi day.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiazi day<ref>That year the seventh month opened on gengwu, so there was no jiazi day.

sentences.zh: </ref>，車駕出宣平門，當渡橋，汜兵數百人遮橋曰：「此天子非也？

translations.literal: </ref>, the imperial carriage exited Xuancheng Gate and was about to cross the bridge; Guo Si's several hundred soldiers blocked the bridge, saying: "Is this not the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, the imperial carriage left through Xuancheng Gate and was about to cross the bridge when several hundred of Guo Si's soldiers barred the way, crying, "Is this really the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 」車不得前。

translations.literal: " The carriage could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: " The carriage could not move forward.

sentences.zh: 傕兵數百人，皆持大戟在乘輿車前，兵欲交，侍中劉艾大呼曰：「是天子也！

translations.literal: Li Jue's several hundred soldiers all held great halberds before the imperial carriage; the armies were about to clash; Palace Attendant Liu Ai shouted loudly: "It is the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred of Li Jue's men stood before the carriage with great halberds raised. As the two sides were about to clash, Palace Attendant Liu Ai shouted, "It is the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」使侍中楊琦高舉車帷，帝曰：「諸君何敢迫近至尊邪？

translations.literal: " He had Palace Attendant Yang Qi raise the carriage curtain high; the Emperor said: "Gentlemen, how dare you press close upon the Supreme One?!
translations.idiomatic: " He had Palace Attendant Yang Qi lift the carriage curtain high. The emperor said, "How dare you crowd so close upon your sovereign?!

sentences.zh: 」汜兵乃卻。

translations.literal: " Guo Si's soldiers then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Si's soldiers then fell back.

sentences.zh: 既渡橋，士眾皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Having crossed the bridge, officers and masses all cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Once the bridge was crossed, officers and soldiers alike shouted, "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 夜到霸陵，從者皆飢，張濟賦給各有差。

translations.literal: At night they reached Baling; the followers were all hungry; Zhang Ji distributed supplies, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Baling that night. The escort was starving, and Zhang Ji distributed provisions according to rank.

sentences.zh: 傕出屯池陽。

translations.literal: Li Jue went out to camp at Chiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue withdrew to camp at Chiyang.

sentences.zh: 丙寅<ref>丙寅是年七月庚午朔，無丙寅。

translations.literal: On bingyin day<ref>In that year the seventh month opened on gengwu; there was no bingyin day.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day<ref>That year the seventh month opened on gengwu, so there was no bingyin day.

translations.literal: </ref>, Zhang Ji was made Bearer of the Left Hunt General with an office like the Three Ducal Ministers;
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, Zhang Ji was appointed Bearer of the Left Hunt General with ministerial rank equal to the Three Ducal Ministers;

sentences.zh: 郭汜為車騎將軍，楊定為後將軍，楊奉為興義將軍。

translations.literal: Guo Si was made Chariot and Cavalry General; Yang Ding was made Rear General; Yang Feng was made General Who Promotes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si became Chariot and Cavalry General; Yang Ding, Rear General; and Yang Feng, General Who Promotes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 皆封列侯。

translations.literal: All were enfeoffed as ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: All were enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 又以故牛輔部曲董承為安集將軍。

translations.literal: Also, Dong Cheng of the former command of Niu Fu was made General Who Pacifies and Settles.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng, formerly an officer under Niu Fu, was also made General Who Pacifies and Settles.

sentences.zh: 郭汜欲令車駕幸高陵，公卿及濟以為宜幸弘農，大會議之，不決。

translations.literal: Guo Si wished to have the imperial carriage visit Gaoling; the grand ministers and Ji thought it appropriate to visit Hongnong; they held a great assembly to discuss it and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si wanted the emperor to go to Gaoling, while the chief ministers and Zhang Ji argued for Hongnong. A full council was held, but no decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使諭汜曰：「弘農近郊廟，勿有疑也。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent an envoy to instruct Guo Si: "Hongnong is near the suburban shrines—do not harbor doubts."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to tell Guo Si, "Hongnong lies near the imperial shrines. Have no misgivings."

sentences.zh: 」汜不從。

translations.literal: " Guo Si did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Si refused.

sentences.zh: 帝遂終日不食。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon went the whole day without eating.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then fasted for the entire day.

sentences.zh: 汜聞之曰：「可且幸近縣。

translations.literal: Guo Si, hearing this, said: "You may for now visit a nearby county."
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Si heard of this, he said, "Very well—let the emperor go to a nearby county for the time being."

sentences.zh: 」八月，甲辰，車駕幸新豐。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month, on jiachen day, the imperial carriage visited Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth month, on jiachen day, the imperial carriage went to Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 丙子<ref>丙子是年八月己亥朔，無丙子。

translations.literal: On bingzi day<ref>In that year the eighth month opened on jihai; there was no bingzi day.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day<ref>That year the eighth month opened on jihai, so there was no bingzi day.

sentences.zh: </ref>，郭汜復謀脅帝還都郿，侍中种輯知之，密告楊定、董承、楊奉令會新豐。

translations.literal: </ref>, Guo Si again plotted to coerce the Emperor to return the capital to Mei; Palace Attendant Chong Ji learned of it and secretly told Yang Ding, Dong Cheng, and Yang Feng to assemble at Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, Guo Si again plotted to force the emperor back to the old capital at Mei. Palace Attendant Chong Ji learned of it and secretly warned Yang Ding, Dong Cheng, and Yang Feng to gather at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 郭汜自知謀泄，乃棄軍入南山。

translations.literal: Guo Si, knowing his plot had leaked, abandoned his army and entered the South Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si, realizing his plot was exposed, abandoned his troops and fled into the South Mountains.

sentences.zh: 9曹操圍雍丘，張邈詣袁術求救，未至，為其下所殺。

translations.literal: 9 Cao Cao besieged Yongqiu; Zhang Miao went to Yuan Shu to ask for rescue; before arriving, he was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao besieged Yongqiu. Zhang Miao went to Yuan Shu to beg for aid but was killed by his own men before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 10冬，十月，以曹操為兗州牧。

translations.literal: 10 In winter, the tenth month, Cao Cao was made Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Cao Cao was appointed Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 11戊戌，郭汜黨夏育、高碩等謀脅乘輿西行。

translations.literal: 11 On wuxu day, Guo Si's partisans Xia Yu, Gao Shuo, and others plotted to coerce the imperial carriage to go west.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day, Xia Yu, Gao Shuo, and other partisans of Guo Si plotted to force the imperial carriage westward.

sentences.zh: 侍中劉艾見火起不止，請帝出幸一營以避火。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Liu Ai, seeing fires rising without cease, requested the Emperor to go out to one camp to avoid the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Liu Ai, seeing fires breaking out everywhere, urged the emperor to move to one of the camps for safety.

sentences.zh: 楊定、董承將兵迎天子幸楊奉營，夏育等勒兵欲止乘輿，楊定、楊奉力戰，破之，乃得出。

translations.literal: Yang Ding and Dong Cheng led troops to welcome the Son of Heaven to Yang Feng's camp; Xia Yu and the others restrained troops wishing to stop the imperial carriage; Yang Ding and Yang Feng fought hard, broke them, and only then were able to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding and Dong Cheng led troops to escort the emperor to Yang Feng's camp. Xia Yu and the others tried to block the carriage, but Yang Ding and Yang Feng fought them off and at last got the emperor out.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，行幸華陰。

translations.literal: On renyin day, the court traveled to Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day, the court proceeded to Huayin.

sentences.zh: 寧輯將軍段煨具服御及公卿已下資儲，欲上幸其營。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies and Gathers Duan Wei prepared robes, furnishings, and supplies for the grand ministers and below, wishing the Emperor to visit his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wei, General Who Pacifies and Gathers, had prepared robes, provisions, and supplies for the emperor and all the ministers, and invited the court to his camp.

sentences.zh: 煨與楊定有隙，定黨种輯、左靈言煨欲反，太尉楊彪、司徒趙溫、侍中劉艾、尚書梁紹皆曰：「段煨不反，臣等敢以死保。

translations.literal: Wei had a rift with Yang Ding; Ding's partisans Chong Ji and Zuo Ling said Wei wished to rebel; Grand Commandant Yang Biao, Minister over the Masses Zhao Wen, Palace Attendant Liu Ai, and Master of Writing Liang Shao all said: "Duan Wei does not rebel—we dare guarantee it with our lives.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wei and Yang Ding were at odds. Yang Ding's followers Chong Ji and Zuo Ling accused Duan Wei of plotting rebellion. Grand Commandant Yang Biao, Minister over the Masses Zhao Wen, Palace Attendant Liu Ai, and Master of Writing Liang Shao all declared, "Duan Wei is no rebel—we stake our lives on it.

sentences.zh: 」董承、楊定脅弘農督郵令言郭汜來在煨營，帝疑之，乃露次於道南。

translations.literal: " Dong Cheng and Yang Ding coerced the Hongnong Supervisor Postal Commissioner to say that Guo Si had come to Wei's camp; the Emperor was suspicious and encamped in the open south of the road.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Cheng and Yang Ding coerced the Hongnong postal commissioner into reporting that Guo Si was in Duan Wei's camp. The emperor grew suspicious and camped in the open south of the road.

sentences.zh: 丁未，楊奉、董承、楊定將攻煨，使种輯、左靈請帝為詔，帝曰：「煨罪未著，奉等攻之而欲令朕有詔耶？

translations.literal: On dingwei day, Yang Feng, Dong Cheng, and Yang Ding were about to attack Wei; they sent Chong Ji and Zuo Ling to request the Emperor issue an edict; the Emperor said: "Wei's crime is not yet apparent—Feng and the others attack him yet wish to make Us issue an edict?
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day, Yang Feng, Dong Cheng, and Yang Ding prepared to attack Duan Wei. They sent Chong Ji and Zuo Ling to ask the emperor for an edict authorizing the assault. The emperor said, "Duan Wei's guilt is not yet proven, and you would have Us issue an edict to attack him?

sentences.zh: 」輯固請，至夜半，猶弗聽。

translations.literal: " Chong Ji insistently requested; until midnight, still he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong Ji pressed his request until midnight, but the emperor still refused.

sentences.zh: 奉等乃輒攻煨營，十餘日不下。

translations.literal: Feng and the others then on their own authority attacked Wei's camp; more than ten days passed without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng and the others attacked Duan Wei's camp on their own authority, but after more than ten days still could not take it.

sentences.zh: 煨供給御膳，稟贍百官，無有二意。

translations.literal: Wei supplied the imperial meals and provisioned the hundred officials, without a second thought.
translations.idiomatic: All the while Duan Wei continued to supply the emperor's meals and provision the officials, loyal and without wavering.

sentences.zh: 詔使侍中、尚書告諭定等，令與煨和解，定等奉詔還營。

translations.literal: An edict sent the Palace Attendant and Master of Writing to announce to Ding and the others, ordering them to reconcile with Wei; Ding and the others received the edict and returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Palace Attendant and Master of Writing to order Yang Ding and the others to make peace with Duan Wei. They obeyed and withdrew to their camps.

sentences.zh: 李傕、郭汜悔令車駕東，聞定攻煨，相詔共救之，因欲劫帝而西。

translations.literal: Li Jue and Guo Si regretted letting the imperial carriage go east; hearing that Ding was attacking Wei, they summoned each other to rescue him jointly, and thereby intended to seize the Emperor and go west.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Guo Si regretted letting the emperor go east. Hearing that Yang Ding was attacking Duan Wei, they called on each other to intervene—and planned to seize the emperor and carry him west.

sentences.zh: 楊定聞傕、汜至，欲還藍田，為汜所遮，單騎亡走荊州。

translations.literal: Yang Ding, hearing that Li Jue and Guo Si had arrived, wished to return to Lantian; he was blocked by Guo Si; alone on horseback he fled to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding, learning that Li Jue and Guo Si had arrived, tried to retreat to Lantian but was intercepted by Guo Si. He fled alone on horseback to Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 張濟與楊奉、董承不相平，乃復與傕、汜合。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji was not on good terms with Yang Feng and Dong Cheng; he thereupon again joined Li Jue and Guo Si.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, at odds with Yang Feng and Dong Cheng, again threw in his lot with Li Jue and Guo Si.

translations.literal: Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound Ju Jun, wounded, fell from his horse; Li Jue said to those beside him: "Can he still live?
translations.idiomatic: Ju Jun, Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, was wounded and fell from his horse. Li Jue asked his attendants, "Can he still be saved?

sentences.zh: 」儁罵之曰：「汝等凶逆，逼劫天子，使公卿被害，宮人流離。

translations.literal: " Ju cursed them, saying: "You and your kind are violent rebels, forcing and seizing the Son of Heaven, making grand ministers harmed and palace women scattered.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju cursed him: "You violent rebels forced the Son of Heaven into your grasp, murdered the chief ministers, and drove the palace women into exile.

sentences.zh: 亂臣賊子，未有如此也！

translations.literal: Rebellious ministers and traitorous sons—never has there been such as this!
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious ministers and traitorous sons—never has villainy reached such a pitch!

sentences.zh: 」傕乃殺之。

translations.literal: " Li Jue thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Jue had him killed.

sentences.zh: 壬申，帝露次曹陽。

translations.literal: On renshen day, the Emperor encamped in the open at Caoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day, the emperor camped in the open at Caoyang.

sentences.zh: 承、奉乃譎傕等與連和，而密遣間使至河東，招故白波帥李樂、韓暹、胡才及南匈奴右賢王去卑，並率其眾數千騎來，與承、奉共擊傕等，大破之，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Cheng and Feng then deceived Li Jue and the others into joining in peace, while secretly sending covert agents to Hedong to recruit the former White Wave chieftains Li Yue, Han Xian, and Hu Cai, and the Southern Xiongnu Right Worthy King Qubie; all led their masses of several thousand riders to come; together with Cheng and Feng they attacked Li Jue and the others, routed them utterly, and beheaded several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng and Yang Feng feigned peace with Li Jue and his allies while secretly sending agents to Hedong to summon the former White Wave chieftains Li Yue, Han Xian, and Hu Cai, and the Southern Xiongnu Right Worthy King Qubie. They all came at the head of several thousand horsemen. Together with Dong Cheng and Yang Feng they struck Li Jue's forces and routed them, taking several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 於是董承等以新破傕等，可復東引。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dong Cheng and the others, having newly broken Li Jue and the others, could again lead eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by their fresh victory over Li Jue, Dong Cheng and the others resolved to march east again.

sentences.zh: 傕等復來戰，奉等大敗，死者甚於東澗。

translations.literal: Li Jue and the others came again to fight; Feng and the others were greatly defeated; the dead were even more than at East Ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his allies attacked again. Yang Feng and the others were routed, and the dead outnumbered even those lost at East Ravine.

sentences.zh: 光祿〔勳〕鄧淵、廷尉宣璠、少府田芬、大司農張義皆死<ref>光祿〔勳〕鄧淵據章注及《後漢書．獻帝紀》補。

translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness [of Merit], Xuan Fan, Commandant of Justice, Tian Fen, Minister Steward, and Zhang Yi, Grand Minister of Agriculture, all perished<ref>Deng Yuan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness [of Merit], added per Zhang's commentary and the Annals of Emperor Xian in the Book of Later Han.

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Zhao Wen, Chamberlain for Ceremonials Wang Jiang, Commandant of the Guards Zhou Zhong, and Colonel of the Regionally Inspector Guan He were blocked by Li Jue and he wished to kill them; Jia Xu said: "These are all high ministers—how can you harm them?!
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Zhao Wen, Chamberlain for Ceremonials Wang Jiang, Commandant of the Guards Zhou Zhong, and Regional Inspector Guan He were intercepted by Li Jue, who meant to kill them. Jia Xu said, "These are great ministers of state—how can you harm them?!

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " He thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Jue desisted.

sentences.zh: 李樂曰：「事急矣，陛下宜御馬。

translations.literal: Li Yue said: "The situation is urgent; Your Majesty ought to mount a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yue said, "Matters are desperate, Your Majesty—you ought to take horse."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「不可捨百官而去，此何境哉！

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "I cannot abandon the hundred officers and leave—what kind of realm would this be!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "I cannot forsake my ministers and flee—what manner of kingdom would that leave!"

sentences.zh: 」兵相連綴四十里，方得至陝，乃結營自守。

translations.literal: " The soldiers strung together in succession for forty li before they finally reached Shan, where they encamped and held their position.
translations.idiomatic: The troops strung out for forty li before reaching Shan; there they pitched camp and held their ground.

sentences.zh: 時殘破之餘，虎賁、羽林不滿百人，傕、汜兵繞營叫呼，吏士失色，各有分散之意。

translations.literal: At this time, of what remained after the ravages, the Tiger Guard and Feathered Forest Guard numbered fewer than a hundred; the soldiers of Li Jue and Guo Si circled the camp shouting; officials and soldiers turned pale, each with the thought of scattering.
translations.idiomatic: In the wreckage that remained, fewer than a hundred Tiger Guard and Feathered Forest troops still stood. Li Jue and Guo Si's soldiers circled the camp, howling; officers and men turned ashen, each ready to bolt.

sentences.zh: 李樂懼，欲令車駕御船過砥柱，出孟津。

translations.literal: Li Yue was afraid and wished to have the imperial carriage take ship past Distributary Rock and exit at Meng Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yue, in fear, proposed that the imperial carriage go by boat past Distributary Rock and out through Meng Ford.

sentences.zh: 楊彪以為河道險難，非萬乘所宜乘；

translations.literal: Yang Biao regarded the river route as perilous and difficult—not what the ruler of ten thousand chariots ought to travel;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao held that the river passage was treacherous and unfit for an emperor's travel;

sentences.zh: 乃使李樂夜渡，潛具船，舉火為應。

translations.literal: so he had Li Yue cross by night, secretly prepare boats, and raise fires as a signal.
translations.idiomatic: so he sent Li Yue across by night, had boats prepared in secret, and kindled fires as a signal.

sentences.zh: 上與公卿步出營，皇后兄伏德扶后，一手挾絹十匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor walked out of the camp with the high ministers; the Empress's elder brother Fu De supported the Empress, with ten bolts of silk tucked under one arm.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor walked out of the camp with the chief ministers. The Empress's elder brother Fu De supported her, ten bolts of silk under one arm.

sentences.zh: 董承使符節令孫徽從人間斫之，殺旁侍者，血濺後衣。

translations.literal: Dong Cheng had Bearer of the Insignia Sun Hui cut it through from among the people, killing attendants at the side; blood splashed on the Empress's robes.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng ordered Sun Hui, Bearer of the Insignia, to hack the silk apart in the crowd; attendants were killed, and blood spattered the Empress's gown.

sentences.zh: 河岸高十餘丈，不得下，乃以絹為輦，使人居前負帝，餘皆匍匐而下，或從上自投，冠幘皆壞。

translations.literal: The riverbank was more than ten zhang high and they could not descend; so they made a litter from the silk, had men go ahead carrying the Emperor, and the rest all crawled down on hands and knees—or threw themselves from above; caps and headcloths were all ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The bank rose more than ten zhang; no one could climb down. They fashioned a litter from the silk and had men carry the Emperor ahead while the rest crawled or threw themselves over the edge. Caps and headbands were torn to rags.

sentences.zh: 既至河邊，士卒爭赴舟，董承、李樂以戈擊之，手指於舟中可掬。

translations.literal: When they reached the river, soldiers scrambled for the boats; Dong Cheng and Li Yue struck them with halberds—fingers in the boats could be scooped up.
translations.idiomatic: At the river, soldiers surged for the boats. Dong Cheng and Li Yue beat them back with halberds; fingers piled in the hulls until one could scoop them up by the handful.

sentences.zh: 帝乃御船。

translations.literal: The Emperor then boarded the boat.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor boarded at last.

sentences.zh: 同濟者，皇后及楊彪以下才數十人，其宮女及吏民不得渡者，皆為兵所掠奪，衣服俱盡，發亦被截，凍死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Those who crossed together were only the Empress and a few dozen from Yang Biao downward; palace women and officials and commoners who could not cross were all plundered by the soldiers—clothes stripped entirely, hair shorn as well; those who froze to death were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Empress and a few dozen from Yang Biao down crossed with him. Palace women, officials, and commoners left behind were plundered by the troops—stripped to the skin, hair cut off; frozen corpses littered the banks beyond count.

sentences.zh: 衛尉士孫瑞為傕所殺。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guards Shi Sun Rui was killed by Li Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sun Rui, Commandant of the Guards, was slain by Li Jue.

sentences.zh: 傕見河北有火，遣騎候之，適見上渡河，呼曰：「汝等將天子去邪！

translations.literal: Li Jue saw fire north of the river and sent riders to investigate; just then he saw the Emperor crossing the river and called out: "Are you taking the Son of Heaven away?!
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue saw flames on the north bank and sent scouts. He arrived just as the Emperor was crossing and shouted, "You mean to steal the Son of Heaven away?!"

sentences.zh: 」董承懼射之，以被為幔。

translations.literal: " Dong Cheng feared they would shoot and used a quilt as a screen.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng, fearing arrows, draped a quilt as a shield.

sentences.zh: 毀到大陽，幸李樂營。

translations.literal: They sailed to Dayang and visited Li Yue's camp.
translations.idiomatic: They sailed to Dayang and lodged in Li Yue's camp.

sentences.zh: 河內太守張楊使數千人負米來貢餉。

translations.literal: Henei Administrator Zhang Yang sent several thousand men bearing rice as tribute supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang, Administrator of Henei, sent several thousand men laden with rice as tribute provisions.

sentences.zh: 乙亥<ref>乙亥《後漢書．獻帝紀》同作「乙亥」，《後漢紀》作丁亥，與《後漢書》均繫於十二月。

translations.literal: On yihai day<ref>On yihai day, the Annals of Emperor Xian in the Book of Later Han likewise reads "yihai"; the Annals of Later Han reads dinghai, and both the Book of Later Han and that work place the event in the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day<ref>Both the Annals of Emperor Xian in the Book of Later Han and this text read "yihai"; the Annals of Later Han reads dinghai, and both works date the event to the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 按是年十一月戊辰朔，無乙亥，有丁亥。

translations.literal: According to the calendar, that year's eleventh month opened on wuchen; there was no yihai day, but there was a dinghai day.
translations.idiomatic: By the calendar that year, the eleventh month opened on wuchen—there was no yihai day, though dinghai did occur.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁酉朔，無丁亥，也無乙亥。

translations.literal: The twelfth month opened on dingyou; there was no dinghai day, and no yihai day either.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth month opened on dingyou; neither dinghai nor yihai appears in that month.

sentences.zh: 或疑乃己亥之誤。

translations.literal: Some suspect it is an error for jihai.
translations.idiomatic: Some suspect the day-name is a scribal error for jihai.

translations.literal: </ref>, the Emperor rode an ox cart and visited Anyi; Hedong Administrator Wang Yi presented silk and cloth as tribute, bestowing it all on the ministers downward; he enfeoffed Yi as a rank marquis.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, the Emperor rode in an ox cart to Anyi. Wang Yi, Administrator of Hedong, presented silk and cloth as tribute, and the Emperor distributed all of it among his ministers and below; Wang Yi was enfeoffed as a rank marquis.

sentences.zh: 〔十二月，庚子〕<ref>〔十二月庚子〕據《後漢紀》補，為農曆十二月初四日。

translations.idiomatic: </ref>, Hu Cai was appointed General Who Conquers the East and Zhang Yang General Who Pacifies the State; both received the imperial insignia and authority to open their own headquarters.

sentences.zh: 其壘壁群帥競求拜職，刻印不給，至乃以錐畫之。

translations.literal: The fortified-camp group commanders all vied for appointments; seal-carving could not keep up—to the point that they drew them with awls.
translations.idiomatic: Every petty warlord in the camps clamored for commissions; seal-carvers could not keep pace—they began inscribing seals with awls.

sentences.zh: 乘輿居棘籬中，門戶無關閉，天子與群臣會，兵士伏籬上觀，互相鎮壓以為笑。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage dwelt within a thorn hedge; doors and gates were not shut; when the Son of Heaven met with his ministers, soldiers lay atop the hedge to watch, restraining one another as a jest.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage stood within a bramble palisade with no gate to close. When emperor and ministers met in council, soldiers sprawled atop the fence to watch, shoving one another for sport.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣太僕韓融至弘農與傕、汜等連和，傕乃放遣公卿百官，頗歸所掠宮人及乘輿器服。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent Grand Coachman Han Rong to Hongnong to negotiate peace with Li Jue, Guo Si, and the others; Li Jue thereupon released the hundred ministers and officials, and largely returned the palace women and imperial carriage regalia they had plundered.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dispatched Grand Coachman Han Rong to Hongnong to treat with Li Jue, Guo Si, and their faction. Li Jue released the chief ministers and officials and returned much of the plundered palace women and imperial equipage.

sentences.zh: 已而糧穀盡，宮人皆食菜果。

translations.literal: Before long grain was exhausted and palace women all ate vegetables and fruits.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the stores were empty, and palace women subsisted on vegetables and fruit.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，張楊自野王來朝，謀以乘輿還雒陽；

translations.literal: On yimao day, Zhang Yang came from Yewang to attend court and proposed returning the imperial carriage to Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day Zhang Yang came from Yewang to court and urged moving the imperial carriage back to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 諸將不聽，楊復還野王。

translations.literal: the generals would not agree, and Yang returned again to Yewang.
translations.idiomatic: the generals refused, and Yang withdrew to Yewang.

sentences.zh: 是時，長安城空四十餘日，強者四散，羸者相食，二三年間，關中無復人跡。

translations.literal: At this time Chang'an had stood empty for more than forty days; the strong had scattered in all directions; the weak had devoured one another; within two or three years there was no longer any trace of people in the Guanzhong region.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an had lain empty for forty-odd days. The strong fled; the weak fed on one another. Within two or three years no human trace remained in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 沮授說袁紹曰：「將軍累葉台輔，世濟忠義。

translations.literal: Ju Shou advised Yuan Shao: "General, for generations your family has served as ministers at the imperial platform, each age advancing loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shou urged Yuan Shao: "General, your house has stood at the imperial center for generations, each age reckoning loyalty and honor.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷播越，宗廟殘毀，觀諸州郡雖外託義兵，內實相圖，未有憂存社稷恤民之意。

translations.literal: Now the court is cast adrift; the ancestral temple lies in ruins; though the various provinces and commanderies outwardly profess righteous armies, inwardly they truly plot against one another—none shows concern to preserve the altars of state or pity the people.
translations.idiomatic: The court wanders in exile; the ancestral temple is broken. The provinces parade as allies of righteousness, yet inwardly they scheme against one another—none spares a thought for the altars of earth and grain or the people's plight.

sentences.zh: 今州域粗定，兵強士附，西迎大駕，即宮鄴都，挾天子而令諸侯，畜士馬以討不庭，誰能御之！

translations.literal: Now your territory is broadly settled; soldiers are strong and officers attached; welcome the Great Carriage from the west, establish the palace at Ye as capital, hold the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords, gather soldiers and horses to punish the disobedient—who could withstand you!
translations.idiomatic: Your domain is largely secure, your armies strong, your men loyal. Welcome the emperor from the west, make Ye your capital, hold the Son of Heaven to command the lords, and muster horse and foot to punish the recalcitrant—who could stand against you!"

sentences.zh: 」潁川郭圖、淳于瓊曰：「漢室陵遲，為日久矣，今欲興之，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: " Yingchuan Guo Tu and Chunyu Qiong said: "The Han house has long declined; to wish to revive it now—is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tu of Yingchuan and Chunyu Qiong objected: "The House of Han has waned for ages. To revive it now—would that not be hard!

sentences.zh: 且英雄並起，各據州郡，連徒聚眾，動有萬計，所謂秦失其鹿，先得者王。

translations.literal: Moreover heroes rise together, each holding his province and commandery, gathering followers, their forces often in the tens of thousands—what they call 'when Qin lost the deer, the first to catch it becomes king.'
translations.idiomatic: Heroes rise on every side, each holding his province, mustering tens of thousands—the old saying: when the empire fell, he who seized it first would rule.

sentences.zh: 今迎天子自近，動輒表聞，從之則權輕，違之則拒命，非計之善者也。

translations.literal: To welcome the Son of Heaven close at hand, every move must be reported in memorials; obey and your authority grows light, disobey and you face charge of defiance—not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Bring the emperor close and every move must be memorialized to him. Obey, and your power thins; defy, and you face the charge of treason—a poor bargain.

sentences.zh: 」授曰：「今迎朝廷，於義為得，於時為宜，若不早定，必有先之者矣。

translations.literal: " Shou said: "To welcome the court now is right in principle and timely in circumstance; if you do not settle this early, someone will surely get there first.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shou replied: "To welcome the court is righteous and timely. Delay, and another will seize the chance first."

sentences.zh: 」紹不從。

translations.literal: " Shao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 12初，丹陽朱治嘗為孫堅校尉，見袁術政德不立，勸孫策歸取江東。

translations.literal: 12 At the beginning—Danyang Zhu Zhi had once served Sun Jian as a commandant; seeing that Yuan Shu's governance lacked moral foundation, he urged Sun Ce to return and seize Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Zhu Zhi of Danyang had served Sun Jian as a commandant. Seeing Yuan Shu's rule devoid of virtue, he urged Sun Ce to go east and reclaim Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 時吳景攻樊能、張英等，歲餘不克，策說術曰：「家有舊恩在東，願助舅討橫江。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Jing was attacking Fan Neng, Zhang Ying, and others, and for more than a year could not overcome them; Ce urged Yuan Shu: "My family has old kindness in the east; I wish to help my maternal uncle attack Hengjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing was besieging Fan Neng and Zhang Ying without success for more than a year. Ce petitioned Yuan Shu: "My clan holds old ties in the east. I ask leave to aid my uncle in crushing Hengjiang.

sentences.zh: 橫江拔，因投本土召募，可得三萬兵，以佐明使君定天下。

translations.literal: Once Hengjiang is taken, I shall recruit on my native ground and raise thirty thousand troops to help Your Excellency settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: If Hengjiang falls, I can recruit at home and raise thirty thousand men to help you master the empire."

sentences.zh: 」術知其恨，而以劉繇據曲阿，王朗在會稽，謂策未必能定，乃許之。

translations.literal: " Yuan Shu knew his resentment, but with Liu Yao holding Qu'a and Wang Lang in Kuaiji, he thought Ce might not succeed—so he consented.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu knew Ce's grievances, yet with Liu Yao holding Qu'a and Wang Lang in Kuaiji, he doubted Ce could prevail—and granted the request.

sentences.zh: 表策為折衝校尉，將兵千餘人、騎數十匹。

translations.literal: He appointed Ce as Colonel Who Breaks the Enemy, with a little more than a thousand troops and several dozen horses.
translations.idiomatic: He commissioned Ce as Colonel Who Breaks the Enemy with a thousand-odd foot and several dozen horse.

sentences.zh: 行收兵，比至歷陽，眾五六千。

translations.literal: As he marched gathering soldiers, by the time he reached Liyang his force numbered five or six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Marching and gathering troops as he went, he reached Liyang with five or six thousand men.

sentences.zh: 時周瑜從父尚為丹陽守，瑜將兵迎之，仍助以資糧。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Yu's father's younger brother Shang was Administrator of Danyang; Yu led troops to welcome him and also supplied provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu's uncle Shang was then Administrator of Danyang; Yu marched out to welcome Ce and furnished grain and stores.

sentences.zh: 策大喜，曰：「吾得卿，諧也！

translations.literal: Ce was greatly pleased and said: "With you, I am well matched!
translations.idiomatic: Ce was delighted. "With you at my side, all falls into place!"

sentences.zh: 」進攻橫江、當利，皆拔之，樊能、張英敗走。

translations.literal: " He advanced to attack Hengjiang and Dangli, both taken; Fan Neng and Zhang Ying were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Hengjiang and Dangli, seized both, and routed Fan Neng and Zhang Ying.

sentences.zh: 策渡江轉鬥，所向皆破，莫敢當其鋒者。

translations.literal: Ce crossed the river and fought in succession; wherever he turned all was broken; none dared meet his edge.
translations.idiomatic: Ce crossed the Yangtze and fought without pause; nowhere could anyone withstand his spear.

sentences.zh: 百姓聞孫郎至，皆失魂魄。

translations.literal: When the common people heard that Lord Sun was coming, all lost their souls.
translations.idiomatic: At word of Lord Sun's approach, commoners lost heart entirely.

sentences.zh: 長吏委城郭，竄伏山草。

translations.literal: District elders abandoned the walled cities and hid in the hills and grass.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates fled their walled towns and hid in hill and thicket.

sentences.zh: 及策至，軍士奉令，不敢虜略，雞犬菜茹，一無所犯，民乃大悅，競以牛酒勞軍。

translations.literal: When Ce arrived, the soldiers obeyed orders and dared not plunder—chickens, dogs, and vegetables none were violated; the people were then greatly pleased and competed to bring oxen and wine to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Ce arrived, his men obeyed strict orders—no pillage, not a chicken or dog or leek disturbed. The people rejoiced and vied to bring cattle and wine to the camp.

sentences.zh: 策為人，美姿顏，能笑語，〔性〕闊達聽受<ref>〔性〕闊達聽受據章注及《吳志．孫策傳》補。

translations.literal: Ce as a man had handsome features and could jest and converse; [character] expansive and receptive in hearing<ref>[character] expansive and receptive in hearing supplemented according to Zhang's commentary and the Biography of Sun Ce in the Records of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce was handsome, quick with a jest, [by nature] open-handed and quick to listen<ref>[By nature] open-handed and quick to listen, added per Zhang's commentary and the Biography of Sun Ce in the Records of Wu.

sentences.zh: </ref>，善於用人，是以士民見者莫不盡心，樂為致死。

translations.literal: </ref>, skilled in employing men; thus those among officials and commoners who saw him all gave their utmost, joyfully dying in his service.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, and skilled at winning men to his cause. Officials and commoners who met him gave their utmost and gladly died in his service.

sentences.zh: 策攻劉繇牛渚營，盡得邸閣糧穀、戰具。

translations.literal: Ce attacked Liu Yao's Niuzhu camp and obtained all the postal-station grain and war equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Ce stormed Liu Yao's camp at Niuzhu and seized all the depot grain and war stores.

sentences.zh: 時彭城相薛禮、下邳相丹陽笮融依繇為盟主，禮據秣陵城，融屯縣南，策皆擊破之。

translations.literal: At that time Pengcheng Chancellor Xue Li and Xiapi Chancellor Danyang Ze Rong relied on Yao as alliance leader; Li held Molin city, Rong was encamped south of the county—Ce attacked and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng Chancellor Xue Li and Xiapi Chancellor Ze Rong of Danyang had taken Liu Yao as their leader; Li held Molin, Rong camped south of the county seat—Ce defeated them both.

sentences.zh: 又破繇別將於梅陵，攻湖孰、江乘，皆下之，進擊繇於曲阿。

translations.literal: He also defeated Yao's separate general at Meiling, attacked Hushu and Jiangcheng, all taken; he pressed the attack on Yao at Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: He routed another of Liu Yao's generals at Meiling, took Hushu and Jiangcheng, and pressed Liu Yao at Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 繇同郡太史慈時自東萊來省繇，會策至，或勸繇可以慈為大將。

translations.literal: Taishi Ci of Yao's same commandery had come from Donglai to visit Yao; just as Ce arrived, some advised Yao that he could make Ci grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci, a fellow townsman of Liu Yao's, had come from Donglai to visit him. When Ce arrived, some urged Liu Yao to appoint Ci chief general.

sentences.zh: 繇曰：「我若用子義，許子將不當笑我邪！

translations.literal: Yao said: "If I used Ziyi, would Xu Zijiang not laugh at me!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao said, "If I made Ziyi my chief general, Xu Zijiang would mock me!"

sentences.zh: 」但使慈偵視輕重。

translations.literal: " He only sent Ci to scout their strength.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ci only to reconnoiter the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 時獨與一騎卒遇策於神亭，策從騎十三，皆堅舊將遼西韓當、零陵黃蓋輩也。

translations.literal: At that time alone with one mounted soldier, Ci encountered Ce at Shen Ting; Ce's following riders were thirteen—all veteran officers Han Dang of Liaoxi, Huang Gai of Lingling, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Ci rode out with a single trooper and met Ce at Shen Ting. Ce had thirteen riders with him—veterans such as Han Dang of Liaoxi and Huang Gai of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 慈便前鬥，正與策對，策刺慈馬，而攬得慈項上手戟，慈亦得策兜鍪。

translations.literal: Ci then advanced to fight; directly he faced Ce; Ce stabbed Ci's horse and pulled away the hand halberd at Ci's neck; Ci also seized Ce's helmet.
translations.idiomatic: Ci charged to the fore and met Ce blade to blade. Ce speared Ci's horse and wrenched the halberd from Ci's grip; Ci snatched Ce's helmet in turn.

sentences.zh: 會兩家兵騎並各來赴，於是解散。

translations.literal: Just then both sides' soldiers and horsemen arrived together, and they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides' reinforcements arrived at once, and the combatants broke apart.

sentences.zh: 繇與策戰，兵敗，走丹徒。

translations.literal: Yao fought Ce and was defeated, fleeing to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao fought Ce, was routed, and fled to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 策入曲阿，勞賜將士，發恩布令，告諭諸縣：「其劉繇、笮融等故鄉部曲來降首者，一無所問；

translations.literal: Ce entered Qu'a, rewarded the officers and soldiers, issued edicts of grace and proclamation, informing the various counties: "Those who are former troops of Liu Yao, Ze Rong, and the others who come to surrender—nothing will be asked;
translations.idiomatic: Ce entered Qu'a, rewarded his officers and men, and issued a proclamation to the counties: "Former followers of Liu Yao, Ze Rong, and the like who come to surrender will not be questioned;

sentences.zh: 樂從軍者，一身行，復除門戶；

translations.literal: those who wish to follow the army—one man per household enlists, and that household is exempted from corvée;
translations.idiomatic: those who wish to serve—one man per household may enlist, and that household will be exempt from corvée;

sentences.zh: 不樂者不強。

translations.literal: those who do not wish to—no compulsion.
translations.idiomatic: those who do not wish to serve will not be forced."

sentences.zh: 」旬日之間，四面雲集，得見兵二萬餘人，馬千餘匹，威震江東。

translations.literal: " Within ten days men gathered from all sides like clouds; visible troops numbered more than twenty thousand, horses more than a thousand; his authority shook Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days men poured in from every quarter. He mustered more than twenty thousand troops and a thousand-odd horses, and his authority shook Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，袁術表策行殄寇將軍。

translations.literal: On bingchen day, Yuan Shu memorialized Ce as Acting General Who Exterminates Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Yuan Shu memorialized Sun Ce as Acting General Who Exterminates Bandits.

sentences.zh: 策將呂範言於策曰：「今將軍事業日大，士眾日盛，而綱紀猶有不整者，範願暫領都督，佐將軍部分之。

translations.literal: Ce's officer Lu Fan said to Ce: "Now General, your enterprise grows daily greater and your troops daily more numerous, yet discipline still has its lapses; Fan wishes temporarily to serve as commander-in-chief and assist the General in organizing them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fan said to Ce: "Your enterprise grows by the day and your forces swell, yet discipline still falters. Fan asks leave to serve temporarily as commander-in-chief and help you put the ranks in order.

sentences.zh: 」策曰：「子衡既士大夫，加手下已有大眾，立功於外，豈宜復屈小職，知軍中細事乎！

translations.literal: " Ce said: "Zihang is already a scholar-official, and moreover already commands a great force and has achieved merit outside—how should he again be lowered to a petty post, knowing the minute affairs of the army!
translations.idiomatic: Ce said, "Zihang is a scholar-official who already commands a great force and has won glory in the field—why should he be reduced to a petty post, minding the army's trifles!"

sentences.zh: 」範曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Fan said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 今捨本土而託將軍者，非為妻子也，欲濟世務也。

translations.literal: Those who now leave their native ground and entrust themselves to the General do so not for wife and children but to aid the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Those who have left their homes to follow you do so not for wife and children but to serve the times.

sentences.zh: 譬猶同舟涉海，一事不牢，即俱受其敗。

translations.literal: It is like sharing a boat crossing the sea—if one thing is not secure, all alike suffer ruin.
translations.idiomatic: We are as men in one boat on the open sea—if one thing fails, all perish together.

sentences.zh: 此亦範計，非但將軍也。

translations.literal: This too is Fan's plan—not for the General alone.
translations.idiomatic: This is Fan's counsel as well—not yours alone to bear.

sentences.zh: 」策笑，無以答。

translations.literal: " Ce laughed, with nothing to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Ce laughed and had no answer.

sentences.zh: 範出，便釋傕，著褲褶，執鞭詣閣下啟事，自稱領都督，策乃授傳，委以眾事。

translations.literal: Fan went out, then doffed his armor, put on trousers and jacket, took whip in hand and went to the gate headquarters to report for duty, styling himself commander-in-chief; Ce then granted him the seal and commission and entrusted him with the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan went out, stripped off his armor, donned field dress, took a whip in hand, and reported for duty at headquarters as commander-in-chief. Ce granted him the seal and commission and entrusted him with military administration.

sentences.zh: 由是軍中肅睦，威禁大行。

translations.literal: From this the army was orderly and harmonious; authority and prohibition were greatly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the army grew disciplined and orderly, and authority was firmly enforced.

sentences.zh: 策以張紘為正議校尉，彭城張昭為長史，常令一人居守，一人從征討，及廣陵秦松、陳端等亦參與謀謨。

translations.literal: Ce appointed Zhang Hong as Colonel of Rectifying Counsel, Pengcheng Zhang Zhao as Chief Clerk, always ordering one to remain in garrison and one to follow on campaigns; Guangling Qin Song, Chen Duan, and others also participated in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Ce appointed Zhang Hong Colonel of Rectifying Counsel and Zhang Zhao of Pengcheng Chief Clerk, always keeping one at headquarters and one on campaign; Qin Song and Chen Duan of Guangling also joined his councils.

sentences.zh: 策待昭以師友之禮，文武之事，一以委昭。

translations.literal: Ce treated Zhao with the courtesy due a teacher and friend; civil and military affairs he wholly entrusted to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Ce treated Zhang Zhao with the courtesy due a teacher and friend and entrusted all civil and military affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 昭每得北方士大夫書疏，專歸美於昭，策聞之，歡笑曰：「昔管子相齊，一則仲父，二則仲父，而桓公為霸者宗。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhao received letters from scholar-officials of the north, they solely praised Zhao; Ce heard and said with delight: "Formerly Guan Zhong served Qi—called first Zhongfu, then again Zhongfu, and Duke Huan became the paragon of hegemons.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhang Zhao received letters from northern scholar-officials, they praised him alone. Ce heard and laughed with delight: "When Guan Zhong served Qi, Duke Huan called him Zhongfu once, then Zhongfu again—and became the paragon of hegemons.

sentences.zh: 今子布賢，我能用之，其功名獨不在我乎！

translations.literal: Now Zibu is worthy—if I can employ him, will his merit and fame not rest on me!
translations.idiomatic: Zibu is worthy, and I can use him—will his glory not be mine as well!

sentences.zh: 袁術以從弟胤為丹陽太守。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu appointed his younger cousin from the father's side Yin as Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu appointed his cousin Yin Administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 周尚、周瑜皆還壽春。

translations.literal: Zhou Shang and Zhou Yu both returned to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shang and Zhou Yu both returned to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 劉繇自丹徒將奔會稽，許劭曰：「會稽富實，策之所貪，且窮在海隅，不可往也。

translations.literal: Liu Yao was about to flee from Dantu to Kuaiji; Xu Shao said: "Kuaiji is rich and substantial—the very thing Ce covets—and moreover lies poor at the sea's edge; you must not go.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao was about to flee from Dantu to Kuaiji. Xu Shao said, "Kuaiji is rich and strong—the very prize Ce covets—and it lies trapped at the sea's edge. You must not go there.

sentences.zh: 不如豫章，北達豫壤，西接荊州；

translations.literal: Better Yuzhang—it reaches north to the lands of Yu, west joins Jing Province;
translations.idiomatic: Better Yuzhang—it opens north onto the lands of Yu and west onto Jing Province;

sentences.zh: 若收合吏民，遣使貢獻，與曹兗州相聞，雖有袁公路隔在其間，其人豺狼，不能久也。

translations.literal: if you gather officials and people, send envoys with tribute, and establish contact with Cao Zhoumu, even though Yuan Gonglu stands between them—that man is a wolf and cannot long endure.
translations.idiomatic: if you rally officials and people, send tribute envoys, and open contact with Cao of Yan Province. Though Yuan Gonglu stands between you, that wolf cannot endure for long.

sentences.zh: 足下受王命，孟德、景升必相救濟。

translations.literal: Your lordship holds the king's mandate—Mengde and Jingsheng will surely rescue and aid you.
translations.idiomatic: You hold the king's commission—Mengde and Jingsheng will surely come to your aid.

sentences.zh: 」繇從之。

translations.literal: " Yao followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao took his advice.

sentences.zh: 13初，陶謙以笮融為下邳相，使督廣陵、下邳、彭城糧運。

translations.literal: 13 At the beginning—Tao Qian had appointed Ze Rong as Chancellor of Xiapi, ordering him to oversee grain transport for Guangling, Xiapi, and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Tao Qian had appointed Ze Rong Chancellor of Xiapi and charged him with grain transport for Guangling, Xiapi, and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 融遂斷三郡委輸以自入，大起浮屠祠，課人讀佛經，招致旁郡好佛者至五千餘戶。

translations.literal: Rong thereupon cut off the three commanderies' supply shipments for his own use, greatly built Buddhist shrines, compelled people to read Buddhist sutras, and drew good Buddhists from neighboring commanderies to more than five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Rong diverted the three commanderies' grain shipments to his own use, built great Buddhist temples, compelled people to recite sutras, and drew more than five thousand Buddhist households from neighboring commanderies.

sentences.zh: 每浴佛，輒多設飲食，布席於路，經數十里，費以巨億計。

translations.literal: Every Buddha-bathing day he invariably set out abundant food and drink, spread mats along the road for several tens of li, the expense reckoned in the hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: On every Buddha-bathing festival he laid out feasts along the road for tens of li, the cost reckoned in the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 及曹操擊破陶謙，徐土不安，融乃將男女萬口走廣陵，廣陵太守趙昱待以賓禮。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao broke Tao Qian and Xu Province was unsettled, Rong then led ten thousand men and women to flee to Guangling; Guangling Administrator Zhao Yu received him with guest courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao defeated Tao Qian and Xu Province fell into turmoil, Rong fled to Guangling with ten thousand people. Zhao Yu, Administrator of Guangling, received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 先是彭城相薛禮為陶謙所逼，屯秣陵，融利廣陵資貨，遂乘酒酣殺昱，放兵大掠，因過江依禮，既而復殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier Pengcheng Chancellor Xue Li had been pressed by Tao Qian and encamped at Molin; Rong coveted Guangling's wealth and goods, then while wine was heavy killed Yu, unleashed troops for great plunder, crossed the river to join Li, and afterward killed him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xue Li, Chancellor of Pengcheng, harried by Tao Qian, had encamped at Molin. Coveting Guangling's wealth, Rong killed Zhao Yu in his cups, let his troops plunder freely, crossed the river to join Xue Li, and later killed him too.

sentences.zh: 劉繇使豫章太守朱皓攻袁術所用太守諸葛玄，玄退保西城。

translations.literal: Liu Yao had Yuzhang Administrator Zhu Hao attack Zhuge Xuan, whom Yuan Shu had installed as administrator; Xuan retreated and held West City.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent Zhu Hao, Administrator of Yuzhang, against Zhuge Xuan, whom Yuan Shu had installed as administrator. Xuan withdrew and held West City.

sentences.zh: 及繇溯江西上，駐於彭澤，使融助皓攻玄。

translations.literal: When Yao went upstream west along the river and encamped at Pengze, he had Rong assist Hao in attacking Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao marched up the Yangtze and encamped at Pengze, he sent Ze Rong to aid Zhu Hao against Zhuge Xuan.

sentences.zh: 許劭謂繇曰：「笮融出軍，不顧名義者也。

translations.literal: Xu Shao said to Yao: "Ze Rong takes the field—he is one who cares nothing for reputation and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao warned Liu Yao: "When Ze Rong takes the field, he cares nothing for honor or duty.
