translations.idiomatic: "have him secretly guard against Ze Rong" emended per Zhang's commentary and the commentary to the Biography of Liu Yao in Records of Wu, citing the Spring and Autumn of Emperor Xian.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.literal: </ref>.

sentences.zh: 」融到，果詐殺皓，代領郡事。

translations.literal: " When Rong arrived, he indeed deceived and killed Hao and took over the administration of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ze Rong arrived, he treacherously killed Zhu Hao and assumed control of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 繇進討融，融敗走，入山，為民所殺。

translations.literal: Yao advanced to attack Rong; Rong was defeated and fled, entered the mountains, and was killed by the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao marched against Ze Rong. Rong was defeated and fled into the hills, where local people killed him.

sentences.zh: 詔以前太傅掾華歆為豫章太守。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Hua Xin, former clerk to the Grand Tutor, as Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Hua Xin, formerly a clerk to the Grand Tutor, Administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 丹陽都尉朱治逐吳郡太守許貢而據其郡，貢南依山賊嚴白虎。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhi, Commandant of Danyang, drove out Xu Gong, Administrator of Wu Commandery, and seized that commandery; Gong fled south and relied on the mountain bandit Yan Baihu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhi, Commandant of Danyang, expelled Xu Gong, Administrator of Wu Commandery, and took the commandery for himself. Xu Gong fled south and threw in his lot with the mountain bandit Yan Baihu.

sentences.zh: 14張超在雍丘，曹操圍之急，韓曰：「惟臧洪當來救吾。

translations.literal: 14 Zhang Chao was at Yongqiu; Cao Cao besieged him urgently. Han said: "Only Zang Hong will come to save us.
translations.idiomatic: 14 Zhang Chao held Yongqiu while Cao Cao pressed the siege hard. Han said, "Only Zang Hong will come to our rescue.

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「袁、曹方睦，洪為袁所表用，必不敗好以招禍。

translations.literal: " The crowd said: "Yuan and Cao are just now on friendly terms; Hong has been recommended and employed by Yuan—he will surely not ruin the friendship to invite disaster.
translations.idiomatic: " The others said, "Yuan Shao and Cao Cao are on good terms, and Hong holds office at Yuan Shao's recommendation. He will never break that alliance and bring disaster on himself.

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「子源天下義士，終不背本；

translations.literal: " Chao said: "Ziyuan is a man of righteousness under Heaven; in the end he will not betray his roots;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Chao replied, "Ziyuan is a man of honor throughout the realm. He would never abandon his obligations;

sentences.zh: 但恐見制強力，不相及耳。

translations.literal: I only fear that if constrained by superior force, he may not reach us in time.
translations.idiomatic: I only fear that stronger powers may restrain him and keep him from reaching us in time.

sentences.zh: 」洪時為東郡太守，徒跣號泣，從紹請兵，將赴其難，紹不與；

translations.literal: " Hong was then Administrator of Dong Commandery; barefoot and weeping aloud, he went to Yuan Shao to request troops and was about to go to their rescue, but Shao would not give them;
translations.idiomatic: " Zang Hong was then Administrator of Dong Commandery. Barefoot and weeping, he begged Yuan Shao for troops to march to Zhang Chao's aid, but Shao refused.

sentences.zh: 請自率所領以行，亦不許。

translations.literal: He asked to lead his own command and go, but this too was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to go with only the men under his own command, and that too was denied.

sentences.zh: 雍丘遂潰，張超自殺，操夷其三族。

translations.literal: Yongqiu thereupon fell; Zhang Chao killed himself, and Cao exterminated his clan to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqiu soon fell. Zhang Chao took his own life, and Cao Cao wiped out his clan to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 洪由是怨紹，絕不與通。

translations.literal: Hong therefore resented Shao and broke off all communication with him.
translations.idiomatic: From this Zang Hong nursed a grievance against Yuan Shao and cut off all contact with him.

sentences.zh: 紹興兵圍之，歷年不下。

translations.literal: Shao raised troops and besieged him; year after year he could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao raised an army and besieged him, but the city held out for years.

sentences.zh: 紹令洪邑人陳琳以書喻之，洪復書曰：「僕小人也，本乏志用；

translations.literal: Shao had Hong's fellow townsman Chen Lin write to persuade him. Hong wrote back: "Your servant is a petty man, originally lacking resolve and ability;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao had Chen Lin, a fellow townsman of Zang Hong, write to persuade him. Hong replied, "I am a man of no account, with little talent or ambition to begin with;

sentences.zh: 中因行役，蒙主人傾蓋，恩深分厚，遂竊大州，寧樂今日自還接刃乎！

translations.literal: midway, on account of travel service, I received my patron's tilted-canopy greeting; his grace was deep and our bond thick, and I thereupon usurped a great province—could I rejoice today to turn back and cross blades myself!
translations.idiomatic: then, while traveling on duty, I met a patron who welcomed me as an equal. His kindness was deep and our bond strong, and I came to hold a great province. Would I now take pleasure in turning back to cross blades with him!

sentences.zh: 當受任之初，自謂究竟大事，共尊王室。

translations.literal: When I first received my appointment, I told myself we would see the great enterprise through and together honor the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: When I first took office, I believed we would finish the great work and together uphold the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 豈悟本州被侵，郡將遘厄，請師見拒，辭行被拘，使洪故君遂至淪滅，區區微節，無所獲申，豈得復全交友之道，重虧忠孝之名乎！

translations.literal: Who could have known that my home province would be invaded, my commandery chief meet calamity, my request for troops be refused, and my plea to go be detained, so that Hong's former lord came to ruin—this slight fidelity of mine had no way to be fulfilled. How could I again preserve the way of friendship and once more stain the name of loyalty and filial piety!
translations.idiomatic: Who could have foreseen that my province would be invaded, my commandery chief fall into peril, my plea for troops be refused, and my request to march be denied, until my old lord was destroyed and this small loyalty of mine could never be fulfilled? How could I preserve friendship and still keep the name of loyalty and duty!

sentences.zh: 斯所以忍悲揮戈，收淚告絕。

translations.literal: This is why I swallow grief, raise my spear, wipe away tears, and declare our bond severed.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I choke back grief, take up arms, dry my tears, and break with you.

sentences.zh: 行矣孔璋，足下徼利於境外，臧洪投命於君親；

translations.literal: Go, Kongzhang: you seek profit beyond the borders, while Zang Hong gives his life for lord and kin;
translations.idiomatic: Farewell, Kongzhang. You seek profit abroad, while Zang Hong gives his life for lord and kin.

sentences.zh: 吾子託身於盟主，臧洪策名於長安；

translations.literal: You entrust yourself to the covenant lord; Zang Hong pledged his name at Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: You have attached yourself to the leader of the alliance; I pledged my name at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 子謂余身死而名滅，僕亦笑子生而無聞焉！

translations.literal: You say that I will die and my name be extinguished—I likewise laugh that you live yet leave no renown!
translations.idiomatic: You say I will die forgotten; I say you live without ever being remembered!

sentences.zh: 紹見洪書，知無降意，增兵急攻。

translations.literal: Shao saw Hong's letter and knew he had no intention of surrender; he added troops and pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao read Zang Hong's letter and saw he would not yield, he reinforced the siege and pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 城中糧穀已盡，外無強救，洪自度必不免，呼將吏士民謂曰：「袁氏無道，所圖不軌，且不救洪郡將，洪於大義，不得不死。

translations.literal: Grain in the city was already exhausted and there was no strong relief from outside. Hong judged that he could not escape, called officers, clerks, soldiers, and people, and said: "The Yuan clan is without the Way; what they plot is not legitimate, and they would not save Hong's commandery chief. Hong, for the sake of great righteousness, cannot but die.
translations.idiomatic: When the city's grain was gone and no relief force came, Zang Hong knew he could not survive. He summoned his officers, clerks, soldiers, and people and said, "The Yuan clan is lawless and aims at treason. They refused to save my commandery chief. For honor's sake I cannot but die.

sentences.zh: 念諸君無事空與此禍，可先城未敗，將妻子出。

translations.literal: Considering that you gentlemen have no business empty-handed sharing this disaster, you may, while the city has not yet fallen, take your wives and children out.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear that you should suffer for nothing. While the city still holds, take your wives and children and leave.

sentences.zh: 」皆垂泣曰：「明府與袁氏本無怨隙，今為本朝郡將之故，自致殘困；

translations.literal: " All wept and said: "Your Excellency originally had no grievance with the Yuan clan; now for the sake of this dynasty's commandery chief you have brought ruin upon yourself;
translations.idiomatic: " All wept and said, "Your Excellency had no quarrel with the Yuan clan. You have brought this ruin on yourself for the sake of the dynasty's commandery chief.

sentences.zh: 吏民何忍當捨明府去也！

translations.literal: How can officers and people bear to abandon Your Excellency and leave!
translations.idiomatic: How can your officers and people bear to leave you!

sentences.zh: 」初尚掘鼠煮筋角，後無可復食者。

translations.literal: " At first they still dug up rats and boiled sinews and horns; afterward there was nothing left to eat.
translations.idiomatic: " At first they dug up rats and boiled sinews and horn. In time there was nothing left to eat.

sentences.zh: 主簿啟內廚米三升，請稍以為饘粥，洪歎曰：「何能獨甘此邪！

translations.literal: The chief clerk reported three sheng of rice in the inner kitchen and asked that a little be made into gruel. Hong sighed and said: "How can I alone enjoy this!
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk reported three sheng of rice in the inner kitchen and asked that a little be cooked into gruel. Hong sighed and said, "How can I enjoy this alone!

sentences.zh: 」使作薄糜，遍班士眾，又殺其愛妾以食將士。

translations.literal: " He had thin porridge made and distributed it throughout the army, and also killed his beloved concubine to feed the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " He had thin gruel made and shared it with every soldier, then killed his beloved concubine to feed his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 將士咸流涕，無能仰視者。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers all wept; none could look up.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers wept until none could raise his eyes.

sentences.zh: 男女七八千人，相枕而死，莫有離叛者。

translations.literal: Men and women, seven or eight thousand, died leaning on one another; none deserted.
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight thousand men and women died where they lay, and not one deserted him.

sentences.zh: 城陷，生執洪。

translations.literal: The city fell, and Hong was taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Zang Hong was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 紹大會諸將見洪，謂曰：「臧洪，何相負若此！

translations.literal: Shao held a great assembly of generals to see Hong and said: "Zang Hong, why have you failed me so!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao assembled his generals to confront Zang Hong and said, "Zang Hong, why have you betrayed me like this!

sentences.zh: 今日服未？

translations.literal: Have you submitted today?
translations.idiomatic: Will you submit now?

sentences.zh: 」洪據地瞋目曰：「諸袁事洪，四世五公，可謂受恩。

translations.literal: " Hong braced himself on the ground, glared, and said: "The Yuans served Hong for four generations and five marquisates—one may say I received grace.
translations.idiomatic: " Zang Hong braced himself on the ground, glared, and said, "The Yuan clan owed me much—four generations, five marquisates. I was deeply in their debt.

sentences.zh: 今王室衰弱，無扶翼之意，欲因際會，希冀非望，多殺忠良以立奸威。

translations.literal: Now the royal house is weak; you have no mind to support and assist it. You wish to seize the moment, harbor improper ambitions, and kill many loyal and good men to establish wicked authority.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial house is weak, yet you have no wish to support it. You seize your chance, harbor unlawful ambition, and slaughter loyal men to build a tyrant's power.

sentences.zh: 洪親見呼張陳留為兄，則洪府君亦宜為弟，同共戮力，為國除害，奈何擁眾觀人屠滅！

translations.literal: Hong personally saw you call Zhang of Chenliu 'elder brother'—then Hong's lord also ought to have been your younger brother. We should have joined strength to remove harm for the state—why hold your masses and watch men be slaughtered!
translations.idiomatic: I saw you call Zhang Miao of Chenliu your elder brother, so my lord Zhang Chao should have been your younger brother. We should have joined forces to purge the realm of evil. Instead you held your army back and watched him be destroyed!

sentences.zh: 惜洪力劣，不能推刃為天下報仇，何謂服乎！

translations.literal: It is a pity Hong's strength was inferior and I could not thrust the blade to avenge the realm—what is meant by submitting!
translations.idiomatic: I regret only that I was too weak to strike the blow and avenge the realm. What talk is there of submission!

sentences.zh: 」紹本愛洪，意欲令屈服，原之；

translations.literal: " Shao had originally favored Hong and intended to make him yield and pardon him;
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Shao had once favored Zang Hong and hoped to make him submit and then spare him.

sentences.zh: 見洪辭切，知終不為己用，乃殺之。

translations.literal: seeing Hong's words were stern, he knew in the end Hong would not serve him, and so killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw how fiercely Hong answered, he knew Hong would never serve him, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 洪邑人陳容少親慕洪，時在紹坐，起謂紹曰：「將軍舉大事，欲為天下除暴，而先誅忠義，豈合天意！

translations.literal: Chen Rong of Hong's home district had from youth admired Hong closely; he was then at Shao's gathering, rose, and said to Shao: "General, you undertake a great enterprise and wish to remove violence for the realm, yet you first execute loyalty and righteousness—does this accord with Heaven's intent!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Rong, a fellow townsman of Zang Hong, had admired him since youth. He was present at Yuan Shao's assembly, rose, and said, "General, you claim a great enterprise to purge the realm of tyranny, yet you begin by killing men of loyalty and honor. Does that accord with Heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 臧洪發舉為郡將，奈何殺之！

translations.literal: Zang Hong rose in action for his commandery chief—why kill him!
translations.idiomatic: Zang Hong took up arms for his commandery chief—why kill him!

sentences.zh: 紹慚，使人牽出，謂曰：「汝非臧洪儔，空復爾為！

translations.literal: Shao was ashamed and had men drag him out, saying: "You are not Zang Hong's equal—empty again acting thus!
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Yuan Shao had him dragged out and said, "You are no match for Zang Hong. Why waste your breath!

sentences.zh: 」容顧曰：「仁義豈有常，蹈之則君子，背之則小人。

translations.literal: " Rong looked back and said: "Do benevolence and righteousness have constancy? Tread them and one is a gentleman; turn from them and one is a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Rong looked back and said, "Benevolence and righteousness have no fixed rule. Walk in them and you are a gentleman; turn from them and you are a villain.

sentences.zh: 今日寧與臧洪同日而死，不與將軍同日而生也！

translations.literal: Today I would rather die on the same day as Zang Hong than live on the same day as the General!
translations.idiomatic: Today I would rather die on the same day as Zang Hong than live on the same day as you!

sentences.zh: 」遂復見殺。

translations.literal: " He was then killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: " He too was executed.

sentences.zh: 在坐無不嘆息，竊相謂曰：「如何一日殺二烈士！

translations.literal: Those seated none failed to sigh; privately they said to one another: "How can one day kill two martyrs!
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present sighed, and whispered among themselves, "To kill two martyrs in a single day!

sentences.zh: 15公孫瓚既殺劉虞，盡有幽州之地，志氣益盛，恃其才力，不恤百姓，記過忘善，睚眥必報。

translations.literal: 15 After Gongsun Zan had killed Liu Yu and fully possessed the lands of You Province, his ambition grew ever greater. Relying on his talent and strength, he did not pity the common people; he remembered offenses and forgot kindnesses, and the smallest grudge he must repay.
translations.idiomatic: 15 After Gongsun Zan killed Liu Yu and held all of You Province, his pride swelled. Trusting in his own ability, he cared nothing for the people, remembered every slight and forgot every kindness, and repaid the smallest grudge.

sentences.zh: 衣冠善士，名在其右者，必以法害之；

translations.literal: Gentry and good scholars whose reputation ranked above his he was sure to harm by law;
translations.idiomatic: Any genteel scholar whose reputation outshone his own he destroyed by legal pretext;

sentences.zh: 有材秀者，必抑困使在窮苦之地。

translations.literal: those with outstanding talent he was sure to suppress and constrain, placing them in destitute and bitter places.
translations.idiomatic: any man of outstanding talent he crushed and kept in misery.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，瓚曰：「衣冠皆自以職分當貴，不謝人惠。

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Zan said: "The gentry all consider themselves by office and rank entitled to honor and do not thank others for favors.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Gongsun Zan said, "Men of the gentry think their rank makes them noble and never thank anyone for a kindness.

sentences.zh: 」故所寵愛，類多商販、庸兒，與為兄弟，或結婚姻；

translations.literal: " Therefore those he favored and loved were mostly merchants, peddlers, and common lads; he made brothers of them or formed marriage alliances;
translations.idiomatic: " So those he favored were mostly merchants and common lads. He called them brothers or bound them to him by marriage.

sentences.zh: 所在侵暴，百姓怨之。

translations.literal: wherever they went they invaded and tyrannized; the common people resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they went they plundered and abused the people, who hated them bitterly.

sentences.zh: 劉虞從事漁陽鮮于輔等，合率州兵欲共報仇，以燕國閻柔素有恩信，推為烏桓司馬。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's aide Xianyu Fu of Yuyang and others jointly led provincial troops wishing together to avenge him. Because Yan Province's Yan Rou had long possessed grace and trust, they recommended him as Wuhuan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Fu of Yuyang, an aide to Liu Yu, and others rallied the provincial troops to avenge him. Because Yan Rou of Yan Province was widely trusted, they made him Wuhuan Commandant.

sentences.zh: 柔招誘胡、漢數萬人，與瓚所置漁陽太守鄒丹戰于潞北，斬丹等四千餘級。

translations.literal: Rou recruited and enticed several tens of thousands of barbarians and Han; with Zou Dan, Administrator of Yuyang whom Zan had installed, he fought north of Lu and beheaded Dan and others, more than four thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rou rallied tens of thousands of barbarians and Han troops and fought Zou Dan, Gongsun Zan's appointee as Administrator of Yuyang, north of Lu. More than four thousand heads were taken, including Dan's.

sentences.zh: 烏桓峭王亦率種人及鮮卑七千餘騎，隨輔南迎虞子和與袁紹將麴義，合兵十萬共攻瓚，破瓚於鮑丘，斬首二萬餘級。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan Qiao King also led his tribesmen and more than seven thousand Xianbei horsemen, followed Fu south to welcome Liu Yu's son He, and together with Yuan Shao's general Qu Yi united an army of one hundred thousand to attack Zan jointly; they defeated Zan at Baoqiu and beheaded more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan chieftain Qiao Wang also led his tribesmen and more than seven thousand Xianbei horsemen south with Xianyu Fu to welcome Liu Yu's son Liu He. Together with Yuan Shao's general Qu Yi they mustered one hundred thousand men, defeated Gongsun Zan at Baoqiu, and took more than twenty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 於是代郡、廣陽、上谷、右北平各殺瓚所置長吏，復與鮮于輔、劉和兵合，瓚軍屢敗。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dai Commandery, Guangyang, Shanggu, and Youbeiping each killed the chief officials Zan had installed; again joining forces with Xianyu Fu and Liu He, Zan's army was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Then Dai, Guangyang, Shanggu, and Youbeiping each killed the officials Gongsun Zan had appointed. Joining Xianyu Fu and Liu He again, they defeated Gongsun Zan's army again and again.

sentences.zh: 先是有童謠曰：「燕南垂，趙北際，中央不合大如礪，唯有此中可避世。

translations.literal: Earlier there was a children's song that said: "Yan's southern edge, Zhao's northern border—the center does not meet, large as a whetstone; only within this may one escape the world.
translations.idiomatic: There had been a children's rhyme: "On Yan's southern edge and Zhao's northern border, where the center does not meet, broad as a whetstone—only there can one escape the world.

sentences.zh: 」瓚自謂易地當之，遂徙鎮易，為圍塹十重，於塹裡築京，皆高五六丈，為樓其上；

translations.literal: " Zan considered himself to occupy that place if he changed location; he thereupon moved his headquarters to Yi, dug ten rings of moats, built walled citadels within the moats all five or six zhang high, and erected towers atop them;
translations.idiomatic: " Gongsun Zan decided that place was meant for him and moved his headquarters to Yi. He dug ten rings of moats, built citadels within them five or six zhang high, and raised towers on top.

sentences.zh: 中塹為京，特高十丈，自居焉。

translations.literal: the innermost moat formed a citadel, especially ten zhang high, and he himself dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: The innermost citadel stood ten zhang high, and there he made his home.

sentences.zh: 以鐵為門，斥去左右，男人七歲以上不得入門，專與姬妾居。

translations.literal: He made iron gates, drove away those close to him, and men above seven years of age were not permitted to enter the gate; he dwelt exclusively with concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He set iron gates, drove away his attendants, and barred every male over seven from entering. He lived alone with his concubines.

sentences.zh: 其文簿、書記皆汲而上之。

translations.literal: His documents, registers, and clerical records were all drawn up by rope.
translations.idiomatic: Documents and records were hauled up to him by rope.

sentences.zh: 令婦人習為大聲，使聞數百步，以傳宣教令。

translations.literal: He had women practice shouting loudly so that the voice could be heard for several hundred paces, to transmit and proclaim orders.
translations.idiomatic: He had women practice shouting so their voices carried hundreds of paces and relayed his commands.

sentences.zh: 疏遠賓客，無所親信，謀臣猛將，稍稍乖散。

translations.literal: He kept distant from guests and had none he trusted; plotting ministers and fierce generals gradually drifted apart and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his distance from guests and trusted no one. His strategists and generals gradually deserted him.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，希復攻戰。

translations.literal: From this time onward, he rarely again went to battle.
translations.idiomatic: After that he rarely fought again.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，瓚曰：「我昔驅畔胡於塞表，掃黃巾於孟津，當此之時，謂天下指麾可定。

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Zan said: "I once drove rebellious barbarians beyond the frontier passes and swept the Yellow Turbans at Mengjin; at that time I thought the realm could be settled at a gesture.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Gongsun Zan said, "I once drove the frontier barbarians beyond the passes and swept the Yellow Turbans at Mengjin. Then I thought the realm would fall into my hands at a wave.

sentences.zh: 至於今日，兵革方始，觀此，非我所決，不如休兵力耕，以救凶年。

translations.literal: As for today, arms have just begun—seeing this, it is not for me to decide; better to rest the troops and force farming to relieve a famine year.
translations.idiomatic: Now war has only just begun. Seeing how things stand, the outcome is not mine to decide. Better to stand down, put the army to farming, and survive this year of famine.

sentences.zh: 兵法，百樓不攻。

translations.literal: In the art of war: against a hundred towers, do not attack.
translations.idiomatic: The art of war says: do not assault a fortress of a hundred towers.

sentences.zh: 今吾諸營樓櫓數十重，積穀三百萬斛。

translations.literal: Now my camps' towers and ramparts are several tens of rings deep, and stored grain is three million hu.
translations.idiomatic: My camps now have dozens of rings of towers and ramparts, and three million hu of grain in store.

sentences.zh: 食盡此穀，足以待天下之事矣。

translations.literal: Eating through this grain is enough to await the affairs of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When this grain is gone, the affairs of the realm will have settled themselves.

sentences.zh: 16南單于於扶羅死，弟呼廚泉立，居于平陽。

translations.literal: 16 The Southern Xiongnu chieftain Yufulei died; his younger brother Huchuquan established himself and dwelt at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: 16 The Southern Xiongnu chieftain Yufulei died. His younger brother Huchuquan succeeded him and established his seat at Pingyang.
